title: Globus Medical (GMED): Building Scale in Musculoskeletal Technology

body_text: Globus Medical (GMED) continues to build scale across spine, orthopedics and enabling technologies, including robotic-assisted surgery. Q2 2026 Worldwide net sales: $789.6 million Year-over-year growth: 5.9% Q1 2026 sales: $759.9 million Q1 year-over-year growth: 27.0% First-half 2026 sales: approximately $1.55 billion That puts Globus on an annualized revenue run rate of more than $3 billion based simply on first-half results. The Robotics Angle What makes Globus particularly interesting from a robotics perspective is that the robot isn't necessarily the end product. Its enabling-technologies strategy connects robotic-assisted surgery with navigation, imaging, instruments and implants. That creates a potential ecosystem: Robot + Navigation + Imaging → Procedures → Implants & Instruments The strategic objective is to use enabling technology to deepen surgeon relationships and ultimately drive greater utilization of the company's broader musculoskeletal portfolio. Management has previously described the goal as making robotic-assisted surgery the standard of care while increasing "robotic account pull-through." Financial Foundation The company's first-quarter results provide additional perspective on the earnings power supporting that investment: Revenue: $759.9M Operating income: $150.4M Net income: $124.3M Diluted EPS: $0.90 Compared with Q1 2025: Revenue increased 27% Operating income increased 55% Net income increased 65% 'Diluted EPS increased 67% The result was an operating margin of approximately 19.8% in Q1. Why It Matters Globus represents a different robotics business model. Rather than depending exclusively on selling robotic systems, the company can potentially benefit from the procedures that occur around its technology. As robotic-assisted surgery expands, Globus has an opportunity to participate through: Robotic and navigation systems Imaging Surgical instruments Spine implants Joint reconstruction Trauma products Regenerative biomaterials That creates the possibility of a recurring economic relationship extending well beyond the initial equipment placement. The bigger takeaway: Globus Medical is becoming a sizable musculoskeletal technology platform, with approximately $1.55 billion of sales in the first half of 2026. Enabling Technology → Surgeon Adoption → Procedures → Implants/Instruments → Recurring Revenue Globus Medical Stats Q2 2026 Revenue $789.6M Q2 Revenue Growth +5.9% H1 2026 Revenue ~$1.55B Q1 Operating Income $150.4M Q1 Operating Margin ~19.8% Q1 Net Income Growth +65% Q1 EPS Growth +67%

title: Online Weight Loss Programs Canada: What to Know | Phoenix
summary: Considering an online weight loss program in Canada? Learn how medical weight management works, eligibility, costs, safety and what to look for.
body_text: If you have been looking for weight loss support online, you have probably noticed how quickly the options add up. There are apps, coaching programs, meal plans, supplements and services that offer access to licensed healthcare providers. That makes one question especially important: what should you actually look for in an online weight loss program in Canada? The safest place to start is not by choosing a prescription treatment yourself. It is by choosing a healthcare service that takes your health history seriously, explains the process clearly and connects you with a licensed healthcare provider who can decide whether prescription treatment is appropriate for you. Quick answer: Canadians can access medical weight management online. A legitimate process should begin with a health assessment, followed by an independent review from a licensed healthcare provider. A prescription is never guaranteed. What is an online medical weight loss program? An online medical weight loss program gives you a way to access weight-management care remotely. Depending on your needs, that care may include a review of your health history, discussion of health behaviours and consideration of prescription treatment when clinically appropriate. Canadian obesity guidance recommends looking beyond body weight alone. Healthcare providers may consider BMI, waist measurements, weight-related health concerns, medical history, current medications, personal goals and other clinical factors when assessing someone for treatment. That is why an online assessment should feel like healthcare, not an online checkout. Can you get weight loss treatment online in Canada? Yes. Virtual healthcare can be used to assess Canadians for weight-management treatment. The healthcare provider is still responsible for reviewing your information and deciding whether treatment is appropriate for your situation. A typical process looks like this: Complete an online health assessment. You provide information about your health history, current medications and weight-management goals. A licensed Canadian healthcare provider reviews your information. There is no automatic prescription and no guarantee that prescription treatment will be recommended. Your provider makes a treatment decision. If treatment is appropriate, the provider can discuss your options and next steps. No in-person visit is required for the standard Phoenix assessment process. Care is handled online, with follow-up available through secure communication. If treatment is prescribed and you choose to proceed, delivery can be arranged discreetly. The important point is that the assessment comes before the prescription decision. How do you know if an online weight loss program is legitimate? A polished website is not enough. Look closely at what happens before and after you sign up. Licensed Canadian healthcare providers A licensed healthcare provider should independently review your health information before any prescription decision is made. A meaningful medical assessment The service should ask about your health history, current medications and relevant medical concerns. Be cautious with any service that appears to promise a prescription before your health information has been properly reviewed. Clear treatment and service pricing Understand what you may be paying for before you begin. Costs can vary depending on the service, the treatment prescribed and your insurance coverage. Phoenix publishes current information on its weight loss pricing page so you can review costs before deciding whether to proceed. Ongoing healthcare-provider support Starting treatment should not end the conversation. You should have a clear way to ask questions, report concerns and discuss how your treatment plan is going. Privacy and discreet delivery Your health information is personal. A virtual healthcare service should clearly explain how your information is handled and how prescribed treatment is delivered. No guaranteed outcomes Weight management is individual. Be cautious of services that promise a specific amount of weight loss, guaranteed results or a prescription for a particular treatment. Who may be eligible for prescription weight management? Eligibility is based on an individual clinical assessment. Current Canadian obesity guidance notes that prescription weight-management treatment may be considered for adults with a BMI of 30 or higher, or a BMI of 27 or higher when adiposity-related health complications are present. The same guidance also emphasizes that BMI should not be used on its own and that central adiposity, health complications, treatment goals and individual circumstances matter. If you want a starting point before speaking with a healthcare provider, you can use the Phoenix BMI Calculator . Your result is a screening measure, not a diagnosis or confirmation that prescription treatment is appropriate. What should you expect from a good online assessment? A good assessment should help a healthcare provider understand the person behind the number on the scale. You may be asked about your medical history, current prescriptions, previous weight-management efforts, allergies, relevant health conditions and your goals for care. Your provider may need additional information before making a treatment decision. This process matters because prescription treatment is not appropriate for everyone. Your provider needs enough information to consider potential risks, interactions and whether another approach may be more suitable. How much does an online weight loss program cost in Canada? There is no single standard price for online weight-management care in Canada. When comparing services, separate the cost of accessing care from the cost of any treatment that may be prescribed. Useful questions include: Is there a fee for the assessment? Are healthcare-provider follow-ups included? Is delivery included if treatment is prescribed? Are there membership or recurring service fees? What will the prescribed treatment cost before insurance? Can documentation be provided for eligible insurance reimbursement? Phoenix offers a $0 online assessment. If treatment is prescribed, pricing is shown before you choose whether to proceed. Does insurance cover weight-management treatment in Canada? Coverage depends on your insurance provider and individual benefits plan. Some plans may cover certain prescribed treatments while others may require additional documentation or exclude them. The best way to know is to check your benefits information or contact your insurer directly. Phoenix does not directly bill insurers. Documentation can be provided to support eligible reimbursement, but coverage is determined by your insurer and plan. Why should the assessment come before choosing a prescription treatment? It is natural to research treatment options before starting care. But a prescription decision should be based on your individual health profile, not on which treatment is receiving the most attention online. Different prescription options can have different indications, contraindications, potential side effects, interactions and other considerations. Your healthcare provider can review those factors with you and decide what, if anything, is appropriate. A better question than “Which treatment should I choose?” is: “What options may be appropriate based on my health history and goals?” What about side effects and safety? All prescription treatments can have potential side effects, and the risks vary by treatment and individual. Your healthcare provider should review important safety information before prescribing and explain what to do if you have concerns after starting treatment. Make sure your provider knows about your current medications, supplements and relevant medical history. Health Canada also warns Canadians to be cautious with unauthorized health products sold online. Products that have not been authorized for sale may be counterfeit, mislabeled, improperly stored or contain unexpected ingredients. Accessing prescription treatment through a legitimate Canadian healthcare pathway helps keep provider assessment and product authorization part of the process. How Phoenix online weight management works Phoenix provides virtual weight-management care for eligible Canadians. Complete a secure online health assessment from home. A licensed Canadian healthcare provider independently reviews your information. If prescription treatment is appropriate, your provider can recommend a treatment plan. A prescription is not guaranteed. If treatment is prescribed and you choose to proceed, Phoenix can arrange free, discreet delivery. You can access ongoing healthcare-provider support through the Phoenix platform. Phoenix weight-management care is available in Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island. Want to explore whether medical weight management may be appropriate for you? Start with the Phoenix weight loss assessment . Frequently asked questions Can I access weight loss treatment online in Canada? Yes. Virtual healthcare services can connect eligible Canadians with licensed healthcare providers for weight-management assessment and care. Prescription treatment is only provided when the reviewing healthcare provider determines it is appropriate. Do I need a prescription for prescription weight-management treatment? Yes. Prescription treatments require a valid prescription from an authorized healthcare provider. Completing an online assessment does not guarantee a prescription. How do I know whether an online weight loss program is legitimate? Look for licensed Canadian healthcare providers, a meaningful health assessment, transparent pricing, clear privacy practices, ongoing provider support and a process that does not guarantee a prescription or a specific result. How much does online weight-management care cost in Canada? Costs vary by service, insurance coverage and the treatment prescribed. Compare assessment fees, follow-up costs, delivery charges, recurring fees and treatment pricing before choosing a service. Will insurance cover weight-management treatment? Coverage depends on your insurance provider and benefits plan. Contact your insurer to confirm eligibility and any documentation requirements. Phoenix does not directly bill insurers, but documentation can be provided to support eligible reimbursement. How do I know if I am eligible? A licensed healthcare provider needs to assess your individual situation. BMI can be one consideration, but it is not the only factor. Your provider may also consider waist measurements, medical history, current medications, weight-related health concerns and treatment goals. Can I choose the prescription treatment I want? You can discuss your preferences and questions with your healthcare provider, but the prescribing decision should be based on your health history, clinical needs, potential risks and whether a particular treatment is appropriate for you. What happens after treatment is prescribed? Ongoing care can include healthcare-provider follow-up, questions about treatment, discussion of side effects and changes to your treatment plan when clinically appropriate. The bottom line If you are comparing online weight loss programs in Canada, look beyond the headline price or the treatment getting the most attention online. Focus on the healthcare process: who reviews your assessment, how treatment decisions are made, what the full costs may be and whether you will have support after treatment begins. A legitimate program should help you understand your options without promising a prescription or a specific result. Ready to see whether Phoenix weight-management care may be appropriate for you? Complete the online assessment . This article is for educational purposes only and does not replace medical advice. Speak with a qualified healthcare provider about your individual circumstances.

title: Andrea Brady Honored as Nonprofit Board Member of the Year
summary: Great Southern's Andrea Brady was named Board Member of the Year by the Springfield Business Journal for her nonprofit board leadership.
body_text: not featured 2026-08-07 8/7/2026 News | Community published 1 Andrea Brady Honored as Nonprofit Board Member of the Year Community Outreach and Development Manager recognized by Springfield Business Journal for years of board leadership across Springfield nonprofits "I want Springfield to be a great place to live... I want to be involved in helping to make that happen." - Andrea Brady Great Southern Bank Andrea Brady, Community Outreach and Development Manager at Great Southern Bank, was recently named Board Member of the Year by the Springfield Business Journal as part of its Nonprofit Excellence Awards. The recognition celebrates Andrea's long record of board service across the Springfield community, including her work with the Lost & Found Grief Center, the Springfield Business Development Corp., Springfield Innovation Inc., and the Greater Missouri Leadership Foundation, along with her involvement in Rotary. In an interview with SBJ , Andrea shared that she rarely turns down a chance to help, saying that supporting nonprofits has taught her more about her community and given her a greater sense of purpose along the way. She pointed to Great Southern's own Community Matters program as an example of how the bank encourages associates to roll up their sleeves and get involved. Congratulations to Andrea on this well-deserved honor!

body_text: Q2 Revenue of $42.4 million and Net Income of $2.9 million Sustains Consecutive Quarters of Adjusted EBITDA Profitability IRVINE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 6, 2026-- WM Technology, Inc. (“WM Technology” or the “Company”) (OTC: MAPS), a leading marketplace and technology solutions provider to the cannabis industry, today announced its financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. “The cannabis industry is entering a more demanding phase, particularly in established markets where sustained economic and regulatory pressures continue to reshape the competitive landscape,” said Doug Francis, CEO and Chairman of WM Technology. “Weedmaps is responding by strengthening our core marketplace and the value it delivers to consumers and licensed operators, expanding into underpenetrated states and continuing to evaluate adjacent opportunities across the broader cannabis ecosystem that can support our platform’s long-term growth.” “Maintaining a strong and flexible financial foundation remained a key focus during the second quarter as we continued to adapt to evolving market conditions,” said Susan Echard, CFO of WM Technology. “We maintained a strong liquidity position, managed expenses with discipline and continued to align our operating structure with the scale and needs of the business. At the same time, we allocated resources selectively to targeted marketing, product enhancements and automation initiatives designed to improve scalability, increase operating efficiency and strengthen the long-term economics of the business.” Second Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights Revenues for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 were $42.4 million as compared to $44.8 million in the prior year period. The decrease from the prior year period was primarily driven by a challenging operating environment for our customers, who have faced margin compression and cash flow constraints. Average monthly paying clients(1) of 5,040 was down from 5,241 from the prior year period, largely due to churn in more established markets, partially offset by new client acquisitions across certain developing markets. Average monthly revenues per paying client(2) decreased to $2,807 from $2,852 in the prior year period, due to spend declines in established markets driven by continued industry challenges, such as price deflation and ongoing consolidation, partially offset by a positive mixed impact from churn among clients with below-average spend levels. Net income increased to $2.9 million as compared to $2.2 million in the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA(3) decreased to $5.0 million from $11.7 million in the prior year period. Total shares outstanding across Class A and Class V Common Stock were 159.7 million as of June 30, 2026. Cash increased to $60.5 million as of June 30, 2026, as compared to $59.0 million as of June 30, 2025. About WM Technology Founded in 2008, WM Technology operates Weedmaps, a leading cannabis marketplace for consumers, as well as a broad set of eCommerce and compliance software solutions for cannabis businesses and brands in U.S. state-legal markets. WM Technology holds a strong belief in the power of cannabis and the importance of enabling safe, legal access to consumers worldwide. Over the past 18 years, the Weedmaps marketplace has become a premier destination for cannabis consumers to discover and browse cannabis-related products, access daily dispensary deals, order ahead for pick-up and delivery by participating retailers (where applicable) and learn about the plant. The Company also offers eCommerce-enablement tools designed to help cannabis retailers and brands reach consumers, create business efficiency, and manage industry-specific compliance needs. Headquartered in Irvine, California, the Company is committed to advocating for full U.S. legalization, industry-wide social equity, and continued education about the plant through key partnerships and cannabis subject matter experts. body_text: San Diego’s coastal climate makes outdoor living a way of life in “America’s Finest City.” With mild temperatures year-round and more than its share of sunny days, a pool becomes a natural extension of your home, equally suited to relaxed afternoons, weekend get-togethers or a quick swim before dinner (without having to shake off any sand). While San Diego offers beautiful beaches, scenic neighborhoods and a laid-back coastal culture, there’s something incredibly appealing about having your own private retreat just steps from your back door. An exquisitely designed pool offers a space to unwind, entertain and enjoy a slice of the good life – whether you live in North County, East County or points in between. In many San Diego neighborhoods, pools are a coveted feature that can enhance both lifestyle and long-term home value. For homeowners planning to stay, the return on your investment is less a matter of percentages and more about everyday enjoyment. Whether you’re taking your morning coffee poolside in La Jolla, or spending weekends with family and friends in your La Mesa backyard, an inground swimming pool can be the centerpiece of outdoor living and the backdrop for many memorable moments. At Latham, we pride ourselves on our 70-year reputation for excellence in crafting durable custom pools. Our network of independent builders spans North America and our presence as one of the premier pool companies in San Diego has served countless homeowners with thoughtful design and expert craftsmanship on every project. But what pool is right for you? From sleek fiberglass designs to highly customizable vinyl liner pools or compact plunge pools ideal for smaller spaces, there’s a pool to suit every lifestyle. We’ll help you better understand the different materials, design considerations and custom features to bring your vision to life. Inground Pool Options Inground swimming pools come in a variety of sizes, shapes and materials – each with their own unique attributes. Three of the most popular types of inground pools are: Fiberglass pools. The ultimate in beauty, durability and low-maintenance enjoyment, Latham fiberglass pools are made with a scratch-resistant, algae-resistant gel coat finish that minimizes upkeep and delivers a smooth-to-the-touch feel in a range of dazzling colors. Vinyl liner pools. For a beautifully blank canvas that lets you customize nearly every aspect of your pool, vinyl liner pools are ideal. From the color of your liner to an array of custom features, your pool takes shape according to your preferred aesthetics to bring your vision to life. Plunge pools. Ideal for smaller backyards or when you want a pool that doesn’t dominate the entire space, plunge pools leave you with more room for an outdoor grilling station, a shady pergola or even a homegrown veggie garden. No matter what type of inground pool you choose, Latham offers a range of options to help you create a bespoke pool that works for your lifestyle. Features like variable-speed pumps, algae-resistant finishes, and eco-minded pool covers not only offer a more beautiful backyard experience, but put water conservation and ease of maintenance top-of-mind. Many Latham pool models are autocover-ready, making it easy to add an automatic safety cover that provides both protection and sustainability. Historically, San Diego has been prone to drought and water shortages , making water a precious commodity. Not only can an autocover prevent unauthorized access and protect pets and children from falling in when your pool is unsupervised, but it can also prevent water evaporation, saving natural resources. Every Latham pool and its components are backed by industry-leading warranties , giving you greater peace of mind alongside years of enjoyment. This makes them an appealing choice for homeowners focused on efficiency as well as design aesthetics. Whether you’re taking a quick dip or spending a lazy afternoon wading, comfort is part of the experience, too. The sleek finish is gentle underfoot and won’t snag your swimsuit. Latham fiberglass pools are available in shapes that range from crisp rectangular lines to nature-inspired freeform layouts. Thoughtful features like integrated seating, Baja ledges (sometimes called “tanning ledges”) and slip-proof steps create a space that feels both functional and refined. Its generous Baja ledge can double as a spacious spot to lounge or a shallow play area for little ones to splash. Astoria : Bring a touch of pure indulgence to your backyard. Offered in three sizes (12’ x 28,’ 14’ x 35’ and 16’ x 40’), the Astoria delivers contemporary elegance with versatile features. An integrated spillover spa, swim-up seating and a Baja ledge for lounging make it ideal for lively get-togethers or a relaxing morning swim. Olympia : Available in three sizes, the autocover-ready Olympia combines sleek rectangular lines with multiple entry points for graceful exits and easy access. A built-in Baja ledge enhances the enjoyment whether you’re entertaining or just want to kick back with a good book without getting too wet. Latham’s proprietary Crystite Gel Coat offers unparalleled resistance to fading, staining and scratches. Built-in UV protection keeps your pool looking beautiful through years of sun-drenched San Diego summers. Their single-piece construction also means your Latham fiberglass pool arrives ready-to-install, translating to less disruption to your backyard and you can start enjoying your pool sooner. The curving lines of this freeform semi-above ground vinyl liner pool are complemented by a custom stone coping and raised wall. Plunge Pools Whether you have a smaller backyard or prefer a pool that complements a larger range of amenities in your backyard, space-saving plunge pools are the perfect fit. These compact pools offer full-sized fun in a fun-sized package, giving you plenty of pool to enjoy while scaling back on maintenance and water usage. Latham offers both vinyl plunge pools and fiberglass plunge pools , including: The Enchantment collection : With swim-up seating, multiple points of entry, and a spacious Baja ledge that doubles as a wading area, fiberglass Enchantment plunge pools offer the perfect mix of fun and luxury in a compact package. Milan : Our fiberglass Milan is only 10’ x 16, but packs an array of features into its backyard-friendly size. Autocover-ready and equipped with swim-up seating and non-slip steps, the Milan transforms your backyard into a destination. FAQs The average cost to install a pool in San Diego depends on several factors. The size of your pool, custom features and the layout and geographical features of your backyard all play a role. For instance, if you live in an area with clay soil like Rancho Santa Fe, your builder will need to prepare the site with backfill and drainage features to prevent water from expanding the soil around your pool. Specialized solutions to ensure your pool is properly installed can add to the cost of labor and installation. Custom features like an specially-cut autocover for a freeform pool, LED pool lights, or a Baja ledge can also add to the total cost of your pool. Typically, building a new pool in San Diego can start as low as $50,000 and run upwards of $150,000 for bigger pools with more elaborate features. Building a new residential pool in San Diego requires a building permit and the project must comply with the California Building Code, the California Swimming Pool Safety Act, local zoning requirements and applicable city or county rules. Within the City of San Diego, private pools also need to meet local setback requirements, barrier details, and permitting requirements. As per California’s Title 24 , gas-only pool heaters are no longer allowed for new pools as part of a statewide effort to reduce emissions and energy consumption. Instead, pools must meet specific energy standards that require heat pumps, solar systems, or a hybrid system that incorporates renewable energy. California also requires compliant pool barriers and other drowning-prevention measures. State law specifies that enclosures must be at least 60 inches high , gates must open away from the pool and gates must be self-closing and self-latching. Any openings in pool gates or fencing must not be wide enough for a four-inch diameter sphere to pass through. Additionally, compliant fencing must not have any features that would easily allow a toddler to climb over it and access the pool area without adult supervision. Some properties may also need added review beyond the pool permit itself. In parts of San Diego County, grading, drainage, slope conditions and septic or onsite wastewater systems can affect what is required and which agency must sign off. Additionally, San Diego may also request a geotechnical investigation report prior to breaking ground on a new pool to evaluate soil conditions , including expansive soil, unstable ground, fill materials and more. Some of the most common hurdles San Diego homeowners encounter when building a pool are due to geographic features and ensuring a pool meets regulatory requirements. Sloped lots, limited backyard access, retained soil, setback requirements and proximity to adjacent properties can all influence pool design and construction timelines. The City of San Diego also notes site-specific considerations such as native soils, structural design, and retained soil conditions for certain pool types. San Diego’s diverse terrain is one reason why geotechnical reviews of soil and yard conditions are often a big part of the pool permitting and approval process before construction begins. Areas like Rancho Santa Fe have expansive clay soil that can swell when wet and contract when it dries (like pottery). In other parts of the greater San Diego area, Oceanside and Carlsbad have loose, sandy soil that may require reinforcement and retaining walls to prevent shifting. For some homeowners, the biggest challenge is coordination. Depending on the property, a pool project may involve separate reviews for building, grading and onsite wastewater systems rather than a single batch approval. A well-maintained pool can add between $25,000 and $65,000 to the resale value of a home, or up to 10% higher in some areas. Over 17% of homes in San Diego have a pool, marking it as #8 on the list of US cities with the most swimming pools. Value often depends on the neighborhood, as well as the quality and condition of the pool itself. However, many homeowners see a pool as both a lifestyle investment and a feature that can boost resale appeal when its design complements the property. Even if you’re not planning to sell your home in the near future, a pool can bring significant value through the enjoyment it brings now and for years to come. Some of the most common choices include home equity loans, HELOCs, and unsecured personal loans, depending on how they want to structure repayment. Some homeowners prefer home equity loans for larger projects, while others choose personal loans for a faster approval process. Some builders may also work with lending partners to help simplify financing alongside construction timelines. Latham partners with preferred lenders like LightStream and Lyon Financial, offering more options to help streamline the path to pool ownership. The best fit usually comes down to your credit profile, available equity, and preferences around monthly payments. Comparing loan structure, rates, and repayment terms can you decide on an option that works best for your project. title: Best Revenue Operations Software: AI Tools for RevOps Teams
summary: RevOps teams use these AI tools to automate proposals, speed up RFP responses, and improve win rates without adding headcount. See the full list.
body_text: ‍ Key takeaways Revenue operations software spans the whole revenue engine , so most teams run a stack — a CRM at the core, plus specialized tools for forecasting, conversation data, enrichment, automation, and proposals. AI’s biggest contribution is removing manual work : cleaning records, capturing activity, flagging deal risk, and drafting responses — freeing the team for analysis and strategy. Buy for your biggest bottleneck first. Adding dashboards on top of bad data rarely helps; fixing the data or the slowest workflow usually does. Evaluate on fit, not feature counts : native CRM integration, data governance, scalability, and provable ROI in your motion matter more than a long capability list. Start small and measure. The highest-performing RevOps teams add tools one pain point at a time and prove impact before expanding. How AI is reshaping revenue operations software AI changes RevOps software in five concrete ways, each mapping to a real bottleneck: 1. Cleaner data with less effort. Enrichment and hygiene tools deduplicate records, fill missing fields, and capture activity automatically, so forecasts and reports are built on complete data instead of what reps remembered to log. 2. Earlier, more accurate forecasting. Instead of rolling up rep-submitted guesses, AI models weigh engagement signals and deal velocity to flag slipping deals before they slip. According to McKinsey , sellers spend less than 30% of their time with customers — AI aims to give some of that time back. 3. Insight from conversations. Conversation intelligence turns calls and emails into structured signals — objections, competitor mentions, champion engagement that RevOps can act on at scale. 4. Automated workflows. Routing, handoffs, renewal reminders, and cross-system syncs run without manual steps, reducing the administrative load on the team. 5. Faster, more consistent responses. Proposal, RFP, and security-questionnaire automation drafts first responses from approved content, so the response stage stops being a deal bottleneck. Research consistently links this maturity to growth: Forrester has reported that companies with mature revenue operations functions grow meaningfully faster than those without. The rest of this guide covers the tools making that maturity achievable. Revenue operations software comparison Tool Category Best for Starting price (2026)* Inventive AI Proposal, RFP & SQ automation High-volume RFP/DDQ/SQ response Usage-based Clari Revenue intelligence & forecasting Enterprise forecast accuracy ~$100+/user/mo Forecastio Revenue intelligence & forecasting HubSpot-based deal insight Custom Gong Conversation intelligence Deal risk + coaching ~$108+/user/mo Chorus Conversation intelligence Conversation + contact data Subscription Salesforce (Einstein) CRM & sales AI Salesforce-native AI Tiered editions HubSpot Sales Hub CRM & sales AI All-in-one, mid-market From ~$15/user/mo Clay Data enrichment & hygiene Custom enrichment workflows From ~$149/mo Cognism Data enrichment & hygiene Compliant prospect data Custom Clearbit Data enrichment & hygiene Automatic CRM enrichment Subscription 6sense Intent & pipeline generation Enterprise ABM From ~$25K/yr Warmly Intent & pipeline generation Website visitor intent Free / from ~$700/mo Dealfront Intent & pipeline generation EU-compliant intent Subscription Zapier Workflow automation Fast no-code automation Free / paid tiers Make Workflow automation Complex orchestration Free / paid tiers The best revenue operations software and AI tools in 2026 The tools below are grouped by function. Within each group they’re listed in no particular ranking order — the “best” one depends on your stack, team size, and the problem you’re solving. Pricing is summarized as published in 2026; confirm current figures with each vendor. Revenue intelligence & forecasting These platforms consolidate CRM, activity, and engagement data to predict outcomes, inspect the pipeline, and surface risk. Clari Clari revenue intelligence and forecasting software Clari is a revenue platform focused on forecasting, pipeline inspection, and deal-risk detection across the revenue cycle. It ingests CRM, email, and calendar data to build a unified view of every deal and uses AI to predict outcomes and flag slippage. Key capabilities: AI forecasting, pipeline and deal inspection, quarter-over-quarter trend analysis, scenario modeling. Best for: mid-market and enterprise teams where forecast accuracy drives hiring and board planning. Pricing: custom/enterprise (commonly quoted around $100+/user/mo). Consider if: you want forecasting depth; it assumes reasonably clean CRM data as input. Forecastio Forecastio is an AI-powered revenue intelligence platform for B2B teams on HubSpot. Its AI agents continuously review forecasts, deals, and pipeline health, then surface prioritized insights and recommendations instead of static reports. Key capabilities: multiple forecasting models, automated deal prioritization, pipeline-health monitoring, forecast audit trail. Best for: HubSpot-based teams that want fast implementation and deal-level AI insight. Pricing: custom, based on HubSpot deployment. Consider if: you’re on HubSpot; Salesforce-first orgs may prefer alternatives. Conversation intelligence These tools record and analyze sales conversations to reveal why deals win, lose, or stall. Gong Gong conversation intelligence for revenue operations Gong captures and analyzes calls, meetings, and emails, aggregating patterns across deals to surface risk signals and coaching opportunities. It has expanded into broader revenue intelligence, including forecasting. Key capabilities: call recording and transcription, deal-risk scoring, coaching insights, engagement analytics. Best for: teams that want deal visibility and coaching drawn from real buyer conversations. Pricing: custom/enterprise (commonly quoted around $108+/user/mo). Consider if: reps consistently record calls; value drops if adoption is low. Chorus Chorus (part of ZoomInfo) provides conversation intelligence that transcribes and analyzes calls and meetings, identifying buying signals, objections, and competitor mentions to inform messaging and coaching. Key capabilities: call analytics, sentiment and objection detection, deal and coaching dashboards, CRM sync. Best for: teams already in the ZoomInfo ecosystem wanting conversation data alongside contact data. Pricing: subscription; varies by seats and scope. Consider if: you want conversation insight tied to a broader data platform. CRM & sales AI The system of record, now with embedded AI for productivity and forecasting. Salesforce Sales Cloud (Einstein) Salesforce Einstein revenue operations software Salesforce pairs deep CRM functionality with Einstein AI for predictive insights, automated data entry, and forecasting inside the Salesforce ecosystem. Key capabilities: opportunity scoring, AI-assisted emails, automated CRM updates, forecast modeling. Best for: teams standardized on Salesforce that want native AI without leaving the CRM. Pricing: tiered editions (Starter through Unlimited); advanced AI often as add-ons. Consider if: Salesforce is your system of record; value is tied to that ecosystem. HubSpot Sales Hub HubSpot Sales Hub revenue operations tool HubSpot Sales Hub combines CRM automation with AI-driven lead scoring, engagement automation, and pipeline reporting under one roof. Key capabilities: predictive lead scoring, AI email personalization, workflow automation, pipeline dashboards. Best for: growth-stage and mid-market teams that value ease of use and marketing–sales alignment. Pricing: published tiers — Starter (~$15/user/mo), Professional (~$90/user/mo), Enterprise (~$150/user/mo). Consider if: you want an all-in-one platform; very large, complex forecasting may need specialist tools. See our CRM RFI guide if you’re formally evaluating CRMs. Data enrichment & CRM hygiene Clean, complete records are the foundation every downstream tool depends on. Clay Clay is a flexible data-workflow platform connecting 100+ enrichment providers in a spreadsheet-like interface with waterfall logic and an AI research agent for automated web research. Key capabilities: waterfall enrichment, 100+ data sources, AI research automation, custom list building. Best for: technical RevOps teams that want maximum flexibility to build enrichment pipelines. Pricing: credit-based, from ~$149/mo (consumption scales with workflow complexity). Consider if: you have the appetite to build workflows; there’s a learning curve. Cognism Cognism data enrichment for revenue operations Cognism provides a compliant global B2B database with AI-enhanced intent signals, verified contact data, and enrichment to build and prioritize pipeline. Key capabilities: verified emails and direct dials, intent data, CRM/engagement integrations, lead prioritization. Best for: teams that need compliant, accurate prospect data for outbound and segmentation. Pricing: custom, by data volume and region. Consider if: data quality and coverage are your gap; it’s focused on the top of funnel. Clearbit Clearbit enriches CRM contacts and accounts with firmographic and intent data, improving lead context, segmentation, and scoring. Key capabilities: real-time enrichment, firmographic and technographic data, lead scoring inputs, CRM hygiene. Best for: teams wanting automatic enrichment feeding cleaner segmentation and routing. Pricing: subscription; varies by volume and integrations. Consider if: enrichment is the priority; it complements rather than replaces a CRM. Intent & pipeline generation These tools identify accounts showing buying signals — often before a form fill. 6sense 6sense uses predictive models and intent data to identify in-market accounts and prioritize outreach across the buying group, mapping anonymous research to specific target accounts. Key capabilities: buying-stage prediction, first- and third-party intent, account prioritization, orchestration. Best for: enterprise teams running account-based motions with the budget to match. Pricing: custom/enterprise (often quoted from ~$25K/year). Consider if: you have an established ABM strategy; value is limited without one. Warmly Warmly de-anonymizes website visitors in real time and triggers automated actions — alerts, chat, and outreach — turning site traffic into a pipeline signal. Key capabilities: visitor identification, real-time alerts, automated outreach triggers, CRM/Slack integrations. Best for: teams with meaningful web traffic that want to convert intent into action. Pricing: free tier available; paid orchestration from ~$700/mo. Consider if: you have the traffic; ROI scales with visitor volume. Dealfront Dealfront identifies website visitors and interprets intent signals, enriching accounts to surface active opportunities with a strong EU-compliance focus. Key capabilities: visitor identification, account enrichment, buyer-behavior analytics, GDPR-compliant data. Best for: teams (especially in Europe) wanting compliant early-funnel visibility. Pricing: subscription; plans from SMB to enterprise. Consider if: compliance and EU coverage matter; it’s early-funnel focused. Workflow automation & orchestration The connective tissue that moves data and triggers actions between systems. Zapier Zapier is a no-code automation platform connecting hundreds of applications to sync data, route leads, and automate repetitive tasks without engineering. Key capabilities: thousands of app integrations, no-code workflows, lead routing, notifications. Best for: small and mid-size teams automating processes quickly and affordably. Pricing: free tier; paid plans scale by tasks and features. Consider if: you need breadth and speed; very complex logic may need a heavier tool. Make Make (formerly Integromat) is an automation platform offering multi-step workflows, conditional logic, and data transformations for more complex orchestration. Key capabilities: multi-step scenarios, branching logic, data transformation, broad integrations. Best for: teams needing sophisticated automation as the stack grows. Pricing: free tier; paid plans by operations volume. Consider if: your workflows outgrow simple “if-this-then-that” rules. Proposal, RFP & security-questionnaire automation Late-stage response work — RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, and security questionnaires — is one of the most content-heavy, deadline-driven parts of the revenue cycle. Inventive AI Inventive AI proposal and RFP automation for revenue operations Inventive AI is an autonomous AI agentic platform for responding to RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, and security questionnaires, with humans in the loop for approvals. Its agents read the document, draft answers from approved knowledge, and validate the response, while a Content Governance Agent keeps the underlying content current. Key capabilities: agentic drafting with source citations and confidence scores (it flags “information unavailable” rather than guessing); a Context Engine that tailors answers to the deal; automatic detection of conflicting, outdated, or duplicate content; review-and-approval workflows; connections to SharePoint, Google Drive, Salesforce, Confluence, Notion, and more; SOC 2 Type II compliance. Best for: proposal, bid, presales, and RevOps teams with high RFP, DDQ, or security-questionnaire volume. See how it fits revenue teams and how it approaches proposal software . Pricing: usage-based, aligned to response volume. Reported outcomes (customer case studies): Insider improved win rate from 30% to 50% and cut RFP turnaround ~90% ( case study ); AssetWorks reported 422% ROI ( case study ); MaxVal reported ~90% faster turnaround with no lost weekend hours ( case study ). Consider if: your bottleneck is the response/proposal stage; pair it with the forecasting, CRM, and enrichment tools above for full-funnel coverage. For a broader market view, see this list of proposal automation tools and approaches to RFP knowledge management . Building a stack for a fast-scaling B2B SaaS motion specifically? See our companion guide to AI tools for B2B SaaS revenue teams , which focuses on the seller and GTM workflow rather than the operations function. How to choose revenue operations software How to choose revenue operations software The most common mistake is buying the most impressive demo rather than the tool that fixes your biggest constraint. A simple framework: Start with your bottleneck. If forecasts are unreliable, look at revenue intelligence. If the CRM is full of gaps, start with enrichment and hygiene. If responses slow deals down, look at proposal automation. Solve the highest-cost problem first. Demand native integration. Revenue operations software only helps if it fits where the team already works. Prioritize bi-directional CRM sync, shared data, and minimal manual entry over standalone tools that force context-switching. Weigh security and data governance. RevOps data is sensitive — pricing, pipeline, and compliance answers. Look for role-based permissions, encryption, audit logs, and recognized certifications such as SOC 2. Governance is now a top enterprise buying criterion. Confirm it scales with you. Deal volume, headcount, and complexity grow. Favor tools that support multi-region deployments, role-based access, and collaboration without performance drops. Insist on measurable ROI. Ask for case studies and verifiable numbers tied to a motion like yours — time saved, cycle-time reduction, forecast accuracy, win-rate lift — not feature counts. You can also model expected impact with an ROI calculator before committing. When responses are your constraint, strong proposal win themes plus automation tend to move win rates together. Example RevOps AI stacks by company size There’s no universal stack — maturity and budget shape the right mix. Three illustrative starting points: Startup / early-stage. A CRM (HubSpot), lightweight analytics, basic automation (Zapier), and enrichment (Clearbit). Keeps costs low while establishing clean data and a single source of truth. Mid-market. A CRM (HubSpot or Salesforce), revenue intelligence (Gong or Clari), forecasting (Forecastio), workflow automation, and — for teams with heavy RFP or security-questionnaire load — proposal automation such as Inventive AI. Focused on scaling pipeline and tightening forecasting. Enterprise. Salesforce plus enterprise BI, revenue intelligence (Clari and/or Gong), data hygiene (Cognism/Clearbit), enterprise automation (Make or Workato), intent/ABM (6sense), and proposal automation for high response volume. Emphasis on governance, integration depth, and cross-region alignment. The principle in every case: add tools incrementally, prove ROI from each, then expand. Layering tools before proving value is how stacks get expensive without getting better. Tools like these also help accelerate the pipeline once the data foundation is solid. Common challenges (and how to handle them) Data quality. AI is only as good as its inputs. Audit and clean data before rollout, and favor tools with built-in validation and enrichment so quality is maintained continuously rather than in one-off cleanups. Integration complexity. Tools that don’t connect to your CRM and existing systems create new silos. Prioritize out-of-the-box integrations and confirm bi-directional sync during evaluation. Cost versus ROI. Upfront cost can be hard to justify. Tie the decision to concrete outcomes — hours saved, faster cycles, higher forecast accuracy — and start with the highest-impact use case to prove value quickly. Adoption and change management. New tools change how people work. Communicate clearly, set expectations, roll out in phases, and use early wins to build momentum across the team. The future: AI agents in revenue operations The next step beyond dashboards is agentic RevOps — software that continuously analyzes revenue data, flags issues, and recommends or takes action. Instead of manually reviewing reports, teams increasingly receive proactive input on forecast risk, deal execution, pipeline health, and data quality. BCG frames this as a shift “from prediction to execution,” and Gartner continues to position revenue operations as central to predictable, data-driven growth. Expect AI agents to become a standard layer of revenue operations software — monitoring forecasts, cleaning CRM data, analyzing win/loss, and drafting responses — so teams spend less time on analysis and administration and more on decisions. Conclusion Revenue operations software is no longer optional; it’s the foundation of a predictable, scalable revenue engine. But no single platform does everything well. The strongest RevOps teams assemble a stack that matches their maturity — clean data first, then forecasting, conversation insight, automation, and response tooling — and add each piece only after proving it earns its place. Pick for your bottleneck, insist on integration and governance, and measure impact as you go. If your constraint is the response stage — RFPs, DDQs, and security questionnaires slowing deals down — you can estimate the potential impact of automating it before you commit. Frequently asked questions What is revenue operations software? Revenue operations software unifies sales, marketing, and customer success data and automates work across the customer lifecycle. It typically spans CRM, forecasting and revenue intelligence, conversation intelligence, data enrichment, workflow automation, and proposal or RFP automation, giving teams one source of truth for forecasting, reporting, and execution. What AI tools offer revenue operations automation? Tools across every RevOps category now include AI. Common examples are Clari and Forecastio (forecasting), Gong and Chorus (conversation intelligence), Salesforce Einstein and HubSpot (CRM AI), Clay and Cognism (enrichment), 6sense and Warmly (intent), Zapier and Make (workflow automation), and Inventive AI (proposal, RFP, and security-questionnaire automation). How do I choose the right revenue operations software? Start with your biggest bottleneck, then evaluate native CRM integration, security and data governance, scalability, and provable ROI in a motion like yours. Favor tools that fit where your team already works, and add them incrementally rather than all at once. Can AI replace a revenue operations team? No. AI removes manual work — data cleanup, activity capture, drafting, and monitoring — but RevOps still owns strategy, process design, cross-team alignment, and judgment. The realistic outcome is a smaller share of time spent on administration and a larger share on decisions. What’s the difference between revenue operations tools and sales intelligence tools? Sales intelligence tools focus on a slice of the funnel — usually prospecting, contact data, or conversation analysis. Revenue operations software is broader, coordinating data and workflows across sales, marketing, and customer success for the entire revenue cycle. Sales intelligence tools are often part of a wider RevOps stack. How quickly can teams see ROI from revenue operations software? It varies by tool and starting point, but many teams report measurable impact within the first few months — faster cycles, cleaner data, or higher forecast accuracy. body_text: 2026 Mercedes-Benz SL-Class Reviews, Pricing & Specs Write a review $112,550 to $224,900 Original MSRP 7.5 of 10 expert review -- avg user rating (0 reviews) Pros Stylish design Multiple powertrain options Comfortable Cons Irritating transmission Irritating lack of physical controls 7.5 out of 10 expert review Look & feel 9/10 Technology 8/10 Performance 9/10 Safety 7/10 Form & function 7/10 Cost-effectiveness 5/10 In the shallow pool of convertibles, the SL offers a satisfying blend of performance and luxury. The SL-Class is one of the brightest stars in the Mercedes constellation. From gullwing coupes to posh convertibles, some of the most recognizable designs in Mercedes history have worn the SL badge. The current-generation SL, introduced for the 2022 model year, continues that tradition while taking things in a new direction. For 2026, the ultra-luxury Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series joins the lineup, marking the first time Mercedes has applied the prestigious Maybach badge to an SL. Verdict: The SL is a luxurious convertible that’s easy to live with, and the extravagant Maybach model is a logical addition to the lineup. 9/10 The SL has been offered in both coupe and convertible body styles in the past, but in order to create some separation from the AMG GT coupe, the current generation is a convertible only. It shares a platform with the GT coupe, which is why today’s SL technically isn’t a Mercedes-Benz—it’s badged as either a Mercedes-AMG or a Mercedes-Maybach. The lineup consists of four variants of AMG models—SL 43, SL 55, SL 63, and SL 63 S E Performance—plus the new Maybach SL 680, which is what we tested for this review. Regardless of the badge it wears, the SL is the Platonic ideal of a high-end roadster. It starts with classic long-hood, short-rear-deck proportions shared with the AMG GT coupe, but some of that car’s muscular sculpting has been smoothed out. The SL’s elongated headlights and shark-nose front fascia are the automotive equivalent of using a fan to blow your hair back for a photo shoot. The bodywork is shrink-wrapped over exaggerated round wheel arches, and embellished tumblehome keeps the fairly tall body from feeling slab-sided. Our Maybach SL test car took things even further with a chrome grille, a hood ornament, and 21-inch monoblock forged wheels with a mirror-like finish. These stereotypical trappings of luxury made the SL look like a concept car that had escaped its auto show turntable. And like a designer handbag, the Maybach SL is covered in logos. A repeating Maybach logo pattern is available on both the soft top and the hood, the latter applied with first-of-its-kind hardware that works like a giant inkjet printer. More than 50 exclusive paint colors from Mercedes’ Manufaktur small-batch department are available. Mercedes’ current interior aesthetic makes its cars feel special, and the SL is no different. The large air vents, minimal detailing, and nightclub-worthy ambient lighting are a great modern interpretation of luxury. Our test car also wore Maybach-specific Manufaktur Crystal White Nappa leather upholstery with embossed headrests, plus some Maybach logos on the tops of the doors. Nonetheless, it didn’t feel as elevated from non-Maybach models as the price might suggest, and there was more plastic than we’d like to see in a circa-$200,000 car, including on the steering-wheel rim, which was a very odd choice considering that’s the one surface a driver always touches. 9/10 Mercedes offers no shortage of powertrains with the SL, all with a nine-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. The base AMG SL 43 has a 2.0-liter turbocharged inline-four, which might not seem worthy of the brand's flagship convertible, but it develops 416 horsepower and 369 pound-feet of torque, taking the rear-wheel drive (RWD) SL 43 from 0–60 mph in a claimed 4.6 seconds. The AMG SL 55 brings V8 power and all-wheel drive (AWD). Its twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 develops 469 hp and 516 lb-ft of torque, getting the SL 55 from 0–60 mph in a Mercedes-estimated 3.8 seconds. The AMG SL 63 has the same engine, tuned for 577 hp and 590 lb-ft, shaving 0.3 seconds off the 0–60 mph time. The AMG SL 63 S E Performance pairs the twin-turbo V8 with a complex plug-in hybrid system to produce 805 hp and 1,047 lb-ft of torque, which gets it to 60 mph in just 2.8 seconds. This high-performance model also features a different AWD system from the SL 55 and non-hybrid SL 63, carbon-ceramic brakes, rear-axle steering, and an active anti-roll system for the suspension. Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series models like our test car have the 577-hp engine and AWD like the SL 63, combined with an active anti-roll system and rear-axle steering from the E Performance plug-in hybrid. Maybach-specific damper valves and softer springs dial up ride comfort at the expensive of some handling sharpness, but the Maybach SL still exhibits excellent body control and quick responses. It flows effortlessly through corners while erasing bumps and road imperfections. Mercedes says the Maybach SL will get from 0–60 mph in 4.0 seconds—half a second slower than the equally powerful, but lighter, SL 63. Despite the overall emphasis on refinement, acceleration is still brutal enough to make passengers curse—even with a transmission that tends to hesitate off the line. The AMG Speedshift MCT uses a dedicated starting clutch instead of a torque converter, but it was hard to see the benefit of that in everyday driving, where the SL required a careful application of the throttle to avoid stumbling off the line. 7/10 Convertibles can't be judged like other cars when it comes to practicality. An SL won’t support an active lifestyle, but it excels in the areas that make a convertible easier to live with. The current-generation SL doesn’t have a folding hardtop like the last few generations, but its soft top nonetheless keeps the cabin remarkably quiet when deployed. Raising or lowering the roof takes just 15 seconds and can be done at speeds of up to 37 mph. While this can be done via the touchscreen, Mercedes also included dedicated switches that are easy to find. Graphics in the instrument cluster and a chime also clearly confirm when the roof is completely open or closed. With both the roof and the windows down, ambient noise is low enough to easily carry on a conversation with a passenger. A glass pane between the seats deflects some wind, and the tall body sides and windshield ensure most drivers won’t be sitting with their faces in the air stream. The standard Air Scarf neck heaters make driving in colder weather more pleasant. Heated and ventilated front seats are standard as well, along with adjustable lumbar, side, and shoulder bolstering and massage. The SL may only have two seats, but the available space is fairly generous. So is its 7.5 cubic feet of trunk space considering a Bentley Continental GT Convertible or Porsche 911 Carrera Cabriolet can only hold 4.8 cubic feet of cargo. Both of those are four-seaters with small back seats that can serve as extra storage space, but the SL also has its own storage shelf behind the seats and below the tonneau cover. 8/10 A 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster and an 11.9-inch touchscreen are standard. The cluster has a deep hood to prevent glare when driving with the top down, and the touchscreen tilts for the same reason. The SL’s third-generation Mercedes-Benz User Experience (MBUX) infotainment system incorporates wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, as well as natural-language voice recognition. The main touchscreen was responsive and intuitive, with a simple menu layout based around large icons. Both screens also had sharp graphics, and we particularly liked the multiple instrument-cluster layout options, ranging from traditional round gauges to a more futuristic “Sport” setup. However, we would have traded some screen space for analog climate controls and a volume knob to replace the awkward haptic slider. Thankfully, the Mercedes voice-recognition system is fairly reliable, allowing drivers to do more while keeping their hands on the wheel. Optional tech features included a head-up display, a dashcam, and augmented reality navigation, which shows a video feed with arrows highlighting turns on the infotainment screen when using the native navigation system. An AMG Track Pack that records lap times and data traces is also available for those who plan on taking their SL to the track. An 11-speaker Burmester surround sound system is standard, but buyers can upgrade to a 17-speaker version. Our Maybach SL test car had the optional system, and its sound quality didn’t disappoint, but that’s to be expected in a six-figure car. 7/10 Standard driver-assistance features include automatic emergency braking, forward-collision warning, blind spot monitors, safe-exit assist, lane-keep assist, parking assist, and Pre-Safe, which cinches seatbelts, closes windows, and generally preps for a collision if an imminent one is detected. A surround-view camera is standard, too, but we found the default 3D view to be pretty much useless, as it produced a badly distorted fisheye image. Luckily, there’s a 2D version that maintains separate—and legible—views. Adaptive cruise control is optional, but includes stop-and-go functionality for traffic jams and can automatically adjust to changing speed limits. There’s also a Congestion Emergency Braking feature that specifically looks for jams ahead and will apply the brakes automatically if necessary. Several steering-assist features help with evasive maneuvers and lane changes, or nudge the car back into its lane if another vehicle is detected in a blind spot. Traffic-sign recognition is also available. Safety ratings from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) weren’t available at the time of writing, and low-volume, luxury vehicles such as the SL aren’t a priority for crash testing. 5/10 The turbo-four SL 43 is EPA-rated at 22 mpg combined (19 mpg city, 27 mpg highway). The V8 models live down to expectations at 16 mpg combined, with city and highway ratings of 14 mpg and 21 mpg respectively for the SL 55 and SL 63. The Maybach model loses 1 mpg in the city and highway categories, but we nonetheless managed to better its EPA combined rating with a 17.5-mpg indicated average. Official ratings for the SL 63 S E Performance plug-in hybrid weren’t available at the time of writing, but Mercedes estimates 29 mpg combined (33 mpg city, 25 mpg highway). This high-performance model likely won’t have any meaningful all-electric range, but 29 mpg combined is not bad for a car with 805 hp. Pricing starts at $113,850 for the SL 43 (all prices include a mandatory $1,350 destination charge) and the SL 55 and SL 63 start at $143,600 and $189,200, respectively. From there, it’s another big leap to the $209,250 SL 63 S E Performance and $226,650 Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series. Our test car had an MSRP of $243,950, mostly due to the $9,900 Manufaktur Surf Blue paint and $6,500 Maybach logo pattern on the hood. The SL’s broad price range overlaps with that of the Porsche 911 Carrera Cabriolet, which is more engaging to drive and can also be optioned to a similar level of luxury. It lacks the SL’s flair, but it’s the more sensible choice unless buyers are willing to limit themselves to the four-cylinder SL 43, the only SL variant that significantly undercuts the 911 in price. Conversely, the Aston Martin Vantage Roadster doubles down on emotion with evocative styling and the same twin-turbo V8 that powers most of the SL lineup. However, it’s more sports car than luxury car. Bizarrely, the most expensive SL might be the best value in the lineup. While it definitely feels like a lower-priced platform aspiring to ultra-luxury status, the Maybach SL 680 delivers most of the experience of more bespoke luxury cars such as the Bentley Continental GT Convertible at a lower effective price, because shoppers don’t have to dip into an extensive options list to get a well-equipped car. In this case, it pays to go all in. Published Aug 17, 2026 by Stephen Edelstein Stephen is a freelance automotive journalist covering everything on four wheels. Whether it's a new EV or a full-size pickup truck, he's eager to drive it and tell you all about it in a CarGurus Test Drive Review. Besides contributing to CarGurus, Stephen currently has bylines at Digital Trends, Green Car Reports, and Motor Authority. title: UCLOUDLINK GROUP INC. Announces Receipt of Minimum Bid Price Notice from Nasdaq
summary: HONG KONG, Aug. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- UCLOUDLINK GROUP INC. (“UCLOUDLINK” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: UCL), the world’s first and leading mobile data traffic sharing marketplace, today announced that it has received written notification from the staff of the Listing Qualifications Department
body_text: PDF Version HONG KONG, Aug. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- UCLOUDLINK GROUP INC. (“UCLOUDLINK” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: UCL), the world’s first and leading mobile data traffic sharing marketplace, today announced that it has received written notification from the staff of the Listing Qualifications Department of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) dated August 10, 2026, indicating that for the last 33 consecutive business days, the closing bid price for the Company’s American depositary shares (the “ADSs”) was below the minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share requirement set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1). The Nasdaq notification letter has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company’s ADSs on Nasdaq. Pursuant to the Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), the Company is provided with a compliance period of 180 calendar days, or until February 8, 2027, to regain compliance under the Nasdaq Listing Rules. If at any time during the 180-day compliance period, the closing bid price of the Company’s ADSs is US$1.00 per share or higher for a minimum of ten consecutive business days, Nasdaq will provide the Company written confirmation of compliance and the matter will be closed. In the event the Company does not regain compliance by February 8, 2027, subject to the determination by the staff of Nasdaq, the Company may be eligible for an additional 180-day compliance period. The Nasdaq notification letter does not affect the Company’s business operations, and the Company will take all reasonable measures to regain compliance within the prescribed compliance period. About UCLOUDLINK GROUP INC. UCLOUDLINK is the world’s first and leading mobile data traffic sharing marketplace, pioneering the sharing economy business model for the telecommunications industry. The Company’s products and services deliver unique value propositions to mobile data users, handset and smart-hardware companies, mobile virtual network operators (MVNOs) and mobile network operators (MNOs). Leveraging its innovative cloud SIM technology and architecture, the Company has redefined the mobile data connectivity experience by allowing users to gain access to mobile data traffic allowance shared by network operators on its marketplace, while providing reliable connectivity, high speeds and competitive pricing. body_text: View All News U-Haul Holding Company Reports First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results August 5, 2026 Download (opens in new window) RENO, Nev.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- U-Haul Holding Company (NYSE: UHAL, UHAL.B), parent of U-Haul International, Inc., Oxford Life Insurance Company, Repwest Insurance Company and Amerco Real Estate Company, today reported net earnings available to common shareholders for its first quarter ended June 30, 2026, of $122.9 million, compared with net earnings of $142.3 million for the same period last year. Earnings per share for Non-Voting Shares (UHAL.B) were $0.63 for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 compared to $0.73 for the same period in fiscal 2026. “The pickup and van resale market is tepid, yet we produced a gain on sale this quarter after several quarters of losses. Our U-Haul truck resale team is thoughtfully gaining ground,” stated Joe Shoen, Chairman of U-Haul Holding Company. “The pace of storage unit rent up is increasing and rates are holding. More improvement is needed as we are still completing new storage units faster than we are filling them. We are successfully expanding our U-Haul independent dealer teams. This is a bright spot which will help drive U-Move transactions and fleet utilization.” Highlights of First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results Moving and Storage earnings from operations, before consolidation of the equity in earnings of the insurance subsidiaries, decreased $8.1 million to $234.8 million compared to the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Fleet depreciation expense increased $13.5 million for the first quarter and real estate related depreciation expense increased $5.1 million for the quarter, all compared with the first quarter of fiscal 2026, while net losses from the disposal of retired rental equipment decreased $24.0 million to a net gain of $1.9 million for the first quarter, all compared with the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Moving and Storage earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization adjusted (EBITDA) decreased $8.5 million to $536.7 million compared to the first quarter of fiscal 2026 and for the trailing twelve months for June 30, 2026 decreased $13.0 million to $1,637.3 million compared to the trailing twelve months for June 30, 2025. Self-storage revenues increased $15.9 million, or 6.8% versus the first quarter of fiscal year 2026. Same store occupancy decreased 4.5% to 88.3%, revenue per foot increased 7.6%, and the number of locations qualifying for the pool increased by 71. During the first quarter of fiscal 2027, we added 18 new locations with storage and 1.1 million net rentable square feet (NRSF). We have approximately 12 million NRSF in development or pending. Self-moving equipment rental revenues increased $29.3 million, or 2.8% versus first quarter of fiscal year 2026. Transactions and revenue increased for both our In-Town and One-Way markets compared to the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Compared to the same period last year, we increased the number of Company operated retail locations and independent dealers, along with the number of box trucks in the rental fleet. Other revenue for Moving and Storage increased $1.8 million or 1.2% versus the first quarter of fiscal 2026 due to growth of our U-Box product offering. We continue to expand our breadth and reach of this program through additional warehouse space, moving and storage containers and delivery equipment. Fleet maintenance and repair costs experienced a $4.1 million increase, compared with the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Cash and credit availability at the Moving and Storage segment was $1,348.6 million as of June 30, 2026 compared with $1,479.4 million as of March 31, 2026. During the first quarter of fiscal 2027, we repurchased 248,368 shares of our Voting common stock at a cost of $15.6 million and 584,278 shares of our Non-Voting common stock at a cost of $32.4 million. On June 3, 2026, we declared a cash dividend on our Non-Voting Common Stock of $0.05 per share to holders of record on June 15, 2026. The dividend was paid on June 26, 2026. We are holding our 20 th Annual Virtual Analyst and Investor meeting on Thursday, August 20, 2026 at 11 a.m. Arizona Time (2 p.m. Eastern). This is an opportunity to interact directly with Company representatives through a live video webcast at investors.uhaul.com. A brief presentation by the Company will be followed by a question-and-answer session. Our latest Supplemental financial information is available at investors.uhaul.com. U-Haul Holding Company will hold its investor call for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 on Thursday, August 6, 2026, at 8 a.m. Arizona Time (11 a.m. Eastern). The call will be broadcast live over the Internet at investors.uhaul.com. To hear a simulcast of the call, or a replay, visit investors.uhaul.com. About U-Haul Holding Company U-Haul Holding Company is the parent company of U-Haul International, Inc., Oxford Life Insurance Company, Repwest Insurance Company and Amerco Real Estate Company. U-Haul is in the shared use business and was founded on the fundamental philosophy that the division of use and specialization of ownership is good for both U-Haul customers and the environment. About U-Haul Since 1945, U-Haul has been the No. 1 choice of do-it-yourself movers, with a network of more than 25,000 locations across all 50 states and 10 Canadian provinces. U-Haul Truck Share 24/7 offers secure access to U-Haul trucks every hour of every day through the customer dispatch option on their smartphones and our patented Live Verify technology. Our customers' patronage has enabled the U-Haul fleet to grow to approximately 207,600 trucks, 136,500 trailers and 43,200 towing devices. U-Haul is the third largest self-storage operator in North America and offers 1,147,300 rentable storage units and 100.3 million square feet of self-storage space at owned and managed facilities. U-Haul is the largest retailer of propane in the U.S., and continues to be the largest installer of permanent trailer hitches in the automotive aftermarket industry. U-Haul has been recognized repeatedly as a leading "Best for Vets" employer and was recently named one of the 15 Healthiest Workplaces in America. The Company undertakes no obligation to publish revised forward-looking statements to reflect events or circumstances after the date hereof or to reflect the occurrence of unanticipated events, except as required by law.
