body_text: US remote jobs for Nigerians can change more than your paycheck; they can change how you think about where your career can take you. A few years ago, a friend of mine spent almost two hours every morning commuting to work in Lagos. Then, one afternoon, a message from a company in Texas landed in his inbox. They liked his work, wanted him on the team, and had one question: “Can you work US hours?” He could. That question changed the way he looked at his career. He didn’t need to relocate to America or wait for a visa. He already had the laptop, the internet connection and, most importantly, a skill that a company thousands of kilometres away was willing to pay for. Stories like this are becoming increasingly common. US remote jobs for Nigerians have opened up a global market to professionals who can prove that they can solve problems, communicate clearly and deliver results from anywhere. But there’s a catch. You can’t simply say, “I want to work remotely for a US company.” You need a skill that solves a real business problem. So, what skills should you learn? 10 skills that can help you land US remote jobs for Nigerians The good news is that you don’t have to become a software engineer to work remotely for a US company. Businesses need people who can write, analyse data, manage customers, create content, design products and keep projects moving. Here are 10 skills worth developing. 1. Software development Software development remains one of the strongest routes into US remote jobs for Nigerians. Companies need developers to build websites, mobile applications, APIs, internal tools and AI-powered products. Depending on your interests, you can learn languages and frameworks such as JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, React or Node.js. But don’t stop at learning how to code. Build projects. Put them on GitHub. Explain what you built and the problem it solves. A portfolio that demonstrates your ability can speak louder than a list of programming languages on your CV. 2. Data analysis Businesses collect enormous amounts of data. They need people who can turn that data into useful decisions. That makes data analysis another valuable skill for people pursuing US remote jobs for Nigerians. Start with Excel or Google Sheets, then build your knowledge of SQL and data visualisation tools such as Power BI or Tableau. Python can also help you analyse larger datasets. More importantly, learn how to tell a story with data. Instead of simply saying, “I know SQL,” show how you used data to identify a sales problem, understand customer behaviour or improve a business process. 3. Digital marketing A great product still needs customers. That’s where digital marketing comes in. US companies need marketers who can help them attract, convert and retain customers through channels such as SEO, social media, email, paid advertising and content marketing. If you’re exploring US remote jobs for Nigerians, digital marketing can be particularly attractive because you can demonstrate your ability without waiting for someone to give you a job. Run a small campaign. Grow a social media page. Optimise a website. Write SEO articles. Build an email sequence. Then document the results. Numbers such as “increased website traffic by 40%” or “generated 200 leads” are far more compelling than simply writing “digital marketing” on your CV. 4. UI/UX and product design If you’re naturally drawn to how websites and apps look and work, product design could be your entry point into US remote jobs for Nigerians. Learn tools such as Figma and develop a strong understanding of user research, wireframing, prototyping and usability. However, don’t build a portfolio filled only with pretty screens. Explain your thinking. What problem were you solving? What did you change? Why did you make that design decision? US employers aren’t just hiring someone who can make an attractive interface. They want someone who can make a product easier and more useful for customers. 5. Copywriting and content writing Good writing remains a valuable business skill. Companies need people who can write landing pages, blog posts, email campaigns, product descriptions, social media content and sales copy. If you’re looking for US remote jobs for Nigerians, strong English alone isn’t enough. You need to understand your audience and write with a purpose. For example, learn SEO if you want to write blogs. Learn conversion copywriting if you want to write landing pages. Learn product writing if you want to work with technology companies. Pick a niche and build samples around it. 6. Customer success and customer support Not every remote opportunity requires advanced technical skills. Companies also need people who can communicate with customers, solve problems and make users feel heard. Customer support and customer success can therefore provide another route into US remote jobs for Nigerians. Strong communication, empathy, problem-solving and organisation matter here. You should also become comfortable with tools such as Zendesk, Intercom, HubSpot, Slack and CRM platforms. If possible, show employers examples of how you handled difficult customers, reduced response times or improved customer satisfaction. 7. Project management Great ideas don’t execute themselves. Project managers keep people, deadlines, budgets and deliverables moving in the right direction. They coordinate teams, identify risks and make sure everyone knows what needs to happen next. This makes project management a useful skill for professionals targeting US remote jobs for Nigerians. Learn tools such as Asana, ClickUp, Notion, Jira or Trello. More importantly, learn how to communicate clearly, manage priorities and keep projects organised. You can demonstrate this skill through personal projects too. Organise a community event, manage a content campaign or coordinate a volunteer project, then document the process. 8. Video editing and content creation Every company wants attention online. As brands invest more heavily in TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and short-form video, content creators and video editors have plenty of opportunities to work remotely. For people pursuing US remote jobs for Nigerians, this can be a practical skill to monetise because your portfolio can do most of the talking. Learn tools such as CapCut, Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve. Understand storytelling, hooks, pacing, captions and platform-specific content. Don’t just show employers that you can edit a video. Show them that you understand why people watch one video and scroll past another. 9. Bookkeeping and financial operations Numbers don’t disappear just because a company operates remotely. US businesses need people who can manage invoices, reconcile accounts, track expenses and keep financial records organised. If you have a background in accounting, finance or administration, bookkeeping can be a strong route into US remote jobs for Nigerians. Tools such as QuickBooks and Xero can help you build relevant experience. You should also understand basic US accounting concepts and become comfortable working with financial data. Accuracy matters enormously in this field, so build a reputation for being organised, careful and dependable. 10. AI and automation Here’s the skill category that can make many of the others even more valuable: knowing how to use AI and automation effectively. Companies don’t simply need people who can use ChatGPT. They need people who can identify repetitive work, improve processes and use technology to get better results. Learn how to use AI tools for research, content production, data analysis, customer support and workflow automation. Explore tools such as Zapier, Make and AI assistants alongside the software used in your profession. For example, a marketer who understands AI-assisted research and automation can potentially accomplish more than a marketer who only knows how to schedule social media posts. That’s why AI and automation deserve a place among the most valuable skills for US remote jobs for Nigerians. How to stand out when applying for US remote jobs Learning a skill is only half the equation. You also need to prove that you can use it. Instead of filling your CV with every course you’ve completed, build a portfolio around real outcomes. Create three to five projects that demonstrate what you can do. Then optimise your LinkedIn profile and CV around the role you want. For example, don’t write: “Experienced in social media management.” Write: “Managed social media content that increased Instagram engagement by 65% in six months.” The second statement gives an employer something to evaluate. Also, learn how to communicate across time zones. US companies value people who can work independently, meet deadlines and communicate proactively without needing constant supervision. Finally, don’t apply randomly. Research the company. Understand the role. Tailor your application. Show that you’ve thought about the company’s problem and can help solve it. Where can Nigerians find US remote jobs? Once you’ve developed a marketable skill, start looking in places where international companies actually recruit. LinkedIn, Wellfound, Upwork, We Work Remotely and Remote OK can all be useful starting points. You can also search company career pages directly and reach out to founders or hiring managers at remote-first companies. And remember: networking matters. A referral can get your application noticed before a recruiter ever sees your CV. Don’t forget how you’ll get paid Landing one of the many US remote jobs for Nigerians is exciting. But getting the job is only part of the equation. You also need a reliable way to receive and manage your USD earnings. Imagine spending weeks interviewing, finally receiving an offer and then having to tell your new employer, “I’ll figure out how to receive the money later.” You can avoid that problem by setting up your payment infrastructure before you start applying. With Cleva , you can access USD financial tools designed for Nigerians earning internationally. Whether you’re receiving payments from clients, getting paid by a US company or managing your USD income, having the right financial setup means you’re ready when the opportunity arrives. Frequently asked questions about U.S. remote jobs for Nigerians 1. Can Nigerians work remotely for US companies? Yes. Nigerian professionals can work remotely for US companies when the employer’s hiring arrangement allows international workers or contractors. The specific employment, tax and payment requirements depend on the company’s structure and your working arrangement. 2. What is the best skill for US remote jobs for Nigerians? There isn’t one best skill for everyone. Software development, data analysis, digital marketing, product design, writing, customer success, project management, bookkeeping and AI-related skills can all lead to international remote opportunities. The best choice is usually the skill that matches your strengths, interests and the type of problem you want to solve. 3. Do I need a degree to get a US remote job? Not always. Some professions require specific qualifications, but many remote employers place significant emphasis on practical skills, experience and demonstrated results. A strong portfolio can help you prove what you can do. 4. How can I prepare for US remote jobs from Nigeria? Start by choosing one marketable skill, learning the tools used in that field and building practical projects. Then create a strong CV and LinkedIn profile, build a portfolio and start applying strategically to relevant international roles. Conclusion Your location doesn’t have to define the size of your career. A laptop in Lagos can connect you to a startup in New York. A portfolio built in Abuja can get the attention of a hiring manager in California. And a skill you’ve spent months developing can become the reason a company decides to work with you. That’s the real opportunity behind US remote jobs for Nigerians. You don’t need to learn everything. Pick one valuable skill. Get genuinely good at it. Build proof. Put yourself where international employers can find you. Then make sure you’re ready to get paid when the opportunity comes. With the right skill, the right strategy and a reliable way to manage your USD income, your next job doesn’t have to be limited by geography. Your career can be global, even when you’re working from Nigeria. Sign up on Cleva and get your USD payment setup ready before your next international opportunity comes knocking. Share this article

title: Dragonfly Energy Reports Second Quarter 2026 Preliminary Results
summary: Second Quarter Net Sales In-Line With Guidance; Adjusted EBITDA Above Guidance Cost Reduction Actions Drive $3.0 Million Sequential Improvement in Adjusted EBITDA Announced Acquisition of Dakota Lithium Assets, Broadening Product Portfolio and Expanding Revenue Opportunity Across Key End Markets
body_text: Dragonfly Energy Reports Second Quarter 2026 Preliminary Results August 6, 2026 PDF Version Second Quarter Net Sales In-Line With Guidance; Adjusted EBITDA Above Guidance Cost Reduction Actions Drive $3.0 Million Sequential Improvement in Adjusted EBITDA Announced Acquisition of Dakota Lithium Assets, Broadening Product Portfolio and Expanding Revenue Opportunity Across Key End Markets Provides Third Quarter 2026 Guidance and Reaffirms Target of Positive Adjusted EBITDA at $70M Annual Net Sales Run Rate Heavy-Duty Trucking Revenue Expected to More Than Double Sequentially in Q3 as Fleet Programs Expand Second Quarter 2026 Preliminary Financial Highlights Net sales were $13.2 million. OEM net sales were $8.4 million. Gross Margin was 33.0%. Net Loss Attributable to Common Shareholders was $(5.5) million. Adjusted EBITDA was $(1.6) million. RENO, Nev., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dragonfly Energy Holdings Corp. (Nasdaq: DFLI) (“Dragonfly Energy” or the “Company”), an industry leader in lithium battery technology, today reported its preliminary financial and operational results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. “Second-quarter net sales were in line with our guidance, while Adjusted EBITDA exceeded our expectations as the cost actions implemented earlier this year began to take effect,” commented Dr. Denis Phares, Chief Executive Officer. “Adjusted EBITDA improved $3.0 million as compared to the first quarter of 2026 and $0.6 million year over year despite lower net sales, demonstrating the operating leverage inherent in our improved cost structure.” “In the heavy-duty trucking market, the commercial ramp we have been building began to translate into meaningful revenue as deliveries under the Stevens Transport purchase order commenced during the quarter. As fleets expand deployments following initial pilot programs, we expect revenue from this market to more than double sequentially in the third quarter, with continued growth in the fourth quarter and beyond.” “Subsequent to quarter-end, we acquired the assets of the Dakota Lithium brand, representing a compelling strategic and financial opportunity for Dragonfly,” continued Dr. Phares. “Dakota Lithium is a recognized brand with established customer and distributor relationships across marine, outdoor recreation, powersports, golf cart and other specialty battery markets. The acquisition broadens our overall product portfolio and further diversifies our revenue base beyond our core RV and trucking markets. We expect Dakota to begin contributing meaningful revenue and to be accretive to Adjusted EBITDA starting in the fourth quarter.” "In connection with the transaction, existing lenders amended the Company's debt arrangements, including reducing the minimum cash covenant, converting the next two quarters of interest to paid-in-kind interest, and deferring the Senior Leverage Ratio and Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio covenant requirements until September 2027. Collectively, these amendments are expected to preserve approximately $1 million of near-term liquidity and provide the Company with meaningful additional financial flexibility.” Second Quarter 2026 Preliminary Financial and Operating Results Net Sales by Customer Type (in thousands) Fiscal Quarter Ended June 30, 2026 June 30, 2025 Change (YoY) OEM $8,432 $10,050 -16.1% DTC $4,477 $5,948 -24.7% Licensing Fee $250 $250 0% Net Sales $13,159 $16,248 -19.0% Net sales were $13.2 million, including $8.4 million in OEM net sales and $4.5 million in DTC net sales. OEM net sales declined year over year against an industry backdrop in which RV shipments were down 14.2% through midyear, reflecting continued macroeconomic pressure on industry production volumes. Despite that environment, the Company continued to expand model placements and power system content across its existing OEM partnerships. DTC sales declined due to macroeconomic pressures on consumer demand, as well as negative third-party online commentary regarding certain of our products, which we believe has adversely affected customer sentiment. We have initiated legal proceedings to address this commentary. Gross profit was $4.3 million, with a gross margin of 33.0%, compared to gross profit of $4.6 million and gross margin of 28.3%. The decrease in gross profit was primarily due to lower unit volume of battery and accessory sales, with an offset from a $1.1 million benefit related to tariff refund recognized in cost of sales. Operating Expenses totaled $7.2 million, down from $7.9 million, benefiting from the Company’s cost reduction actions. The Company also continued to advance its previously announced facility consolidation during the second quarter. While the process was not fully completed by quarter-end, the Company expects to complete the principal remaining actions during the third quarter. The Company reported a Net Loss of $(4.4) million and a Net Loss Attributable to Common Shareholders of $(5.5) million, or $(0.43) per diluted share. This compares to a Net Loss and a Net Loss Attributable to Common Shareholders of $(7.0) million, or $(5.77) per share, respectively. Adjusted EBITDA excluding stock-based compensation, changes in the fair market value of our warrants, and other one-time expenses, was $(1.6) million, a $0.6 million improvement compared to a loss of $(2.2) million in the second quarter of 2025. Sequentially, Adjusted EBITDA improved $3.0 million from the $(4.6) million reported in the first quarter of 2026, driven by our cost reduction actions. The second quarter financial and operating results are preliminary and are subject to finalization and adjustment in connection with the review of the financial statements for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and the preparation of the Company’s Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The preliminary financial results included in this press release have been prepared by, and are the responsibility of, the Company’s management. During the course of the preparation of the Company’s financial statements and related notes as of and for the three months ended June 30, 2026, the Company may identify items that would require it to make material adjustments to the preliminary financial results presented herein. As a result, investors should exercise caution in relying on this information and should not draw any inferences from this information. This preliminary financial information should not be viewed as a substitute for full financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP and reviewed by the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm. Summary and Outlook “Looking ahead to the third quarter, we expect continued growth in energy storage content and model integration across our OEM partnerships against a continued soft RV market, and trucking sales to ramp through the balance of the year. Our focus in the near term is on disciplined execution as we build on our expanding commercial foundation, integrate the Dakota Lithium brand, which we expect to begin contributing meaningful revenue in the fourth quarter, and drive operating leverage from our improved cost structure. We remain on track toward our target of Adjusted EBITDA profitability at an annualized net sales run rate of approximately $70 million,” concluded Dr. Phares. Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $( 2.4 ) million* * The Company cannot reconcile its expected adjusted operating EBITDA under “Q3 2026 Guidance” without unreasonable effort because certain items that impact net (loss) income and other reconciling metrics are out of the Company's control and/or cannot be reasonably predicted at this time. Actual results may vary from the guidance and the variations may be material. The third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA outlook reflects two temporary timing factors: continued expense associated with vacated facility space that is actively being marketed for sublease, and incremental operating costs to restore Dakota Lithium’s commercial operations ahead of its expected meaningful revenue contribution beginning in the fourth quarter. Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP measure and should be considered only as supplemental to, and not as superior to, financial measures prepared in accordance with United States generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). Please refer to the reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to its nearest GAAP measure in this release. The Company provides non-GAAP financial measures including EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA as a supplement to GAAP financial information to enhance the overall understanding of the Company’s financial performance and to assist investors in evaluating the Company’s results of operations, period over period. Adjusted non-GAAP measures exclude significant unusual items. Investors should consider these non-GAAP measures as a supplement to, and not a substitute for financial information prepared on a GAAP basis. EBITDA is defined as earnings before interest and other income (expenses), income taxes, and depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as EBITDA adjusted for stock-based compensation, change in fair market value of warrant liabilities, non-recurring costs associated with strategic financing, reverse stock split, litigation and loss on settlement. Adjusted EBITDA is a performance measure that the Company believes is useful to investors and analysts because it illustrates the underlying financial and business trends relating to the Company’s core, recurring results of operations and enhances comparability between periods. Adjusted EBITDA has limitations as an analytical tool, and it should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of net loss or other results as reported under GAAP. Some of these limitations are: Adjusted EBITDA does not reflect the Company’s cash expenditures, future requirements for capital expenditures, or contractual commitments; Adjusted EBITDA does not reflect changes in, or cash requirements for, the Company’s working capital needs; Adjusted EBITDA does not reflect the Company’s tax expense or the cash requirements to pay taxes; Although amortization and depreciation are non-cash charges, the assets being amortized and depreciated will often have to be replaced in the future and Adjusted EBITDA does not reflect any cash requirements for such replacements; Adjusted EBITDA should not be construed as an inference that the Company’s future results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items for which the Company may adjust in historical periods; and Other companies in the industry may calculate Adjusted EBITDA differently than the Company does, limiting its usefulness as a comparative measure. title: ProMIS Neurosciences to Report Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Update on August 13, 2026
summary: Company to host investor conference call and webcast at 4:30 p.m. ET. Cambridge, Massachusetts, Aug. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --…...
body_text: ProMIS Neurosciences to Report Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Update on August 13, 2026 Aug 3, 2026 Download as PDF Company to host investor conference call and webcast at 4:30 p.m. ET. Cambridge, Massachusetts, Aug. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ProMIS Neurosciences Inc. (Nasdaq: PMN), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing antibody therapeutics and vaccines targeting toxic misfolded proteins in neurodegenerative diseases, today announced it will report financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, and provide corporate updates on August 13, 2026. The company will host a conference call and webcast on the same day of August 13, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. ET. Conference Call and Webcast Information: Date: August 13, 2026 Time: 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time Dial-in: 1-877-407-9208 (U.S. Investors) 1-201-493-6784 (International) Conference I.D.: 13761812 CallMe TM : Click Here Webcast: Click Here A replay of the webcast will be available in the Investors section of the ProMIS website following the completion of the call. About ProMIS Neurosciences Inc. ProMIS Neurosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to the discovery and development of therapeutic antibodies and vaccines selective for toxic oligomers associated with the development and progression of neurodegenerative and other misfolded protein diseases. The Company's proprietary target discovery engine, EpiSelect™, has been shown to predict novel targets known as Disease Specific Epitopes (DSEs) on the molecular surface of misfolded proteins that cause neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and Parkinson's disease (PD). ProMIS has offices in Cambridge, Massachusetts (USA) and Toronto, Ontario (CAN). For further information: Visit us at www.promisneurosciences.com Media Contact Maggie Whitney LifeSci Communications mwhitney@lifescicomms.com Investor Relations Contact Carie Pierce VP Investor Relations & External Affairs IR@ProMISNeurosciences.com Source: ProMIS Neurosciences Inc. Released August 3, 2026

title: Cracker Barrel Welcomes Fall with New Crispy Homestyle Chicken Deals, Seasonal Favorites and Free Kids Toy Promotion
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Crispy Homestyle Chicken dishes starting at just $9.99, seasonal breakfast favorites and a free toy with an adult entrée and Kid's Meal give busy families more reasons to slow down and enjoy a meal together this fall LEBANON, Tenn. , Aug. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fall means back to school, back to activities and back to calendars that fill up fast. And when family life gets busier, finding an easy, affordable way to get everyone around the table can matter even more. Beginning August 18, Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® is making those everyday moments a little easier with a new lineup of Crispy Homestyle Chicken Deals starting at just $9.99, alongside other seasonal dishes like Sweet Cream Caramel Apple Pancakes and an assortment of Granny Smith Apple beverages. The limited-time menu brings together the comfort, flavor and value families are looking for this time of year, along with the return of Cracker Barrel's popular Free Kids Toy promotion*, giving guests more reasons to choose Cracker Barrel for an easy dinner, a breakfast worth leaving home for or simply a meal together during a busy week. "Fall can feel like a sprint for families. Between school, practices, activities and everything else packed into the week, getting everyone around the table can feel like a win," said Sarah Moore, Chief Marketing Officer at Cracker Barrel. "We want Cracker Barrel to make that a little easier, with food everyone can get excited about, value families can feel good about and the kind of welcome that lets them simply enjoy being together." An Easier Answer to "What's for Dinner?" Cracker Barrel's signature Crispy Homestyle Chicken is getting a flavorful fall refresh. Guests can enjoy the original hand-breaded favorite as an entrée served with two Country Sides and a choice of warm buttermilk biscuits or corn muffins, or as a sandwich served on a toasted buttermilk bun with pickles, Duke's® Real Mayonnaise and a choice of one Country Side, both available for $9.99 . For those looking to turn up the flavor, the lineup also introduces Loaded creations piled high with craveable toppings and Sauced selections finished with bold flavor-forward finishes, offering an easy answer to the nightly "what's for dinner?" question. The NEW Crispy Homestyle Chicken lineup includes: Loaded Creations NEW Maple Bacon Homestyle Chicken – Crispy Homestyle Chicken topped with melted Colby cheese, crispy bacon, sweet maple glaze and cool ranch drizzle. NEW BBQ Smokestack Homestyle Chicken – Crispy Homestyle Chicken stacked with crispy bacon & fried onions, melted Colby cheese and sweet barbecue sauce. Sauced Selections NEW Nashville Hot Homestyle Chicken – A bold, spicy twist on Crispy Homestyle Chicken featuring Cracker Barrel's signature Nashville Hot. NEW Honey Butter Homestyle Chicken – Crispy Homestyle Chicken drizzled with sweet honey butter for the perfect sweet-and-savory combination. Seasonal Breakfast Worth Waking Up For Fall mornings get a little sweeter with the arrival of new seasonal breakfast favorites. Guests can choose from Sweet Cream Caramel Apple Pancakes or Sweet Cream Caramel Apple French Toast , both topped with Cracker Barrel's signature warm, fried cinnamon apples, rich caramel drizzle and sweet vanilla cream sauce, and served with two eggs plus bacon or smoked sausage patties. Whether it's a weekend breakfast, a family tradition or even breakfast- for dinner, the seasonal lineup gives guests another reason to enjoy one of Cracker Barrel's most-loved occasions. Even More Fall Favorites This latest seasonal menu, available at participating restaurants nationwide from August 18 through October 18, also features a collection of returning guest favorites and new sweet seasonal treats, including: NEW Apple Cobbler Cheesecake and returning favorite, Carrot Cake , for a sweet finish. Seasonal beverages including the returning Granny Smith Apple Tea and Granny Smith Apple Mimosa , alongside the NEW Sweet Honey Latte . A Little More Fun for Family Meals To celebrate the start of a new school year, Cracker Barrel is bringing back its popular Free Kids Toy promotion for a limited time, featuring collectible B'loonie Petz toys. Available August 18 through September 7, while supplies last, Cracker Barrel's youngest fans can receive one of six squishy B'loonie Petz toy characters with the purchase of a dine-in adult entrée and Kid's Meal. Featuring a variety of playful pet-inspired designs, the collectible toys are perfect for kids who love fun surprises and building their collection. As an alternative to the free B'loonie Petz toy, guests can receive $5 off a select retail toy from the Old Country Store , inviting kids to explore the unique toys, gifts and unexpected treasures that make the shopping experience part of the Cracker Barrel tradition. To learn more about Cracker Barrel, the new seasonal offerings or find a nearby location, visit CrackerBarrel.com and be sure to follow Cracker Barrel throughout the season and beyond on Facebook , Instagram and TikTok . *One free Kid's B'loonie Petz toy or up to $5 off a retail toy, exclusive of taxes, with qualifying in store purchase of an adult entrée and Kid's Meal on same check made from 8/18/26 to 9/7/26, excl. online and to go purchases. Limit: Max discount of $30 per check/6 total free toy items per check. Not valid on previous purchases or in combination with other offers or discounts. Has no cash value. Subject to availability. Limit and restrictions apply. Cracker Barrel reserves the right to modify or terminate the offer without notice at any time. Void where prohibited by law. Visit www.crackerbarrel.com to find a location near you and to see a complete list of toys available for the offer. About Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. – rooted in a rich legacy of warmth, generosity, and tradition – is on a mission to bring the goodness of country hospitality to life. Since 1969, when the first store opened in Lebanon, Tenn., Cracker Barrel has been serving up abundant portions of craveable homestyle food and offering one-of-a-kind retail finds. With approximately 660 company-owned Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® locations in 43 states, the brand continues to honor its heritage while welcoming everyone with more than a meal. For more information, visit CrackerBarrel.com . http://crackerbarrel.com/ Contact: Media.relations@crackerbarrel.com View original content to download multimedia: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cracker-barrel-welcomes-fall-with-new-crispy-homestyle-chicken-deals-seasonal-favorites-and-free-kids-toy-promotion-302852874.html SOURCE Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc.

title: Ceragon Reports 2026 Second Quarter Financial Results
summary: Ceragon Reports 2026 Second Quarter Financial Results
body_text: Strong demand in India drives 14% year-over-year revenue growth Rosh Ha’ain, Israel, August 11, 2026 - Ceragon (NASDAQ: CRNT), a leading solutions provider of end-to-end wireless connectivity, today reported its financial results for the second quarter period ended June 30, 2026. Q2 2026 Financial Highlights: Revenues of $93.9 million GAAP Operating income of $0.2 million, non-GAAP operating income of $4.0 million GAAP Net loss of $2.1 million, non-GAAP net income of $1.7 million GAAP EPS of ($0.02) per diluted share, non-GAAP EPS of $0.02 per diluted share Q2 2026 Business Highlights: India – Sequentially higher revenue and strong bookings (approximately $120 million in announced year-to-date bookings in July) have increased visibility for the remainder of 2026; notable interest in E-band solutions North America – Demand remained robust with record quarterly bookings in private networks CEO Doron Arazi commented: “ Our second quarter reflects the benefits of the strategy we've been executing over the past several years. Demand remains healthy across multiple end markets, and we're seeing momentum from both our traditional carrier business and newer growth areas such as private networks and managed services. Just as importantly, the quality of our opportunities and customer engagement, gives us confidence in the outlook for the balance of the year, as described below." “Customer demand remains healthy, and our competitive position continues to improve, despite near-term industry-wide cost and supply chain pressures,” continued Mr. Arazi. “Our E-band solutions are generating particular interest from customers and represent a strong competitive differentiator. Our recent field trial success with our 5G FR2 (mmWave) product for a new Tier 1 North American carrier points to our continued innovation that drives increased demand for our technology. Strong bookings and growing interest from new and existing customers reinforce our confidence in Ceragon’s technology, innovation roadmap, and long-term growth prospects.” Primary Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results: Revenues were $93.9 million, up 14.2% from $82.3 million in Q2 2025. Gross profit was $29.7 million, or a gross margin of 31.7%, compared to gross margin of 34.6% in Q2 2025. GAAP Operating income was $0.2 million compared with $2.2 million for Q2 2025. GAAP Net income (loss) was ($2.1) million, or ($0.02) per diluted share, compared with ($1.3) million, or ($0.01) per diluted share for Q2 2025. Non-GAAP results were as follows : Gross margin was 32.2%, operating profit was $4.0 million, and net income was $1.7 million, or $0.02 per diluted share. Balance Sheet Cash and cash equivalents were $34.8 million on June 30, 2026, compared to $38.4 million on December 31, 2025. For a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP results, see the attached tables. Revenue Breakout by Geography: Q2 2026 · India 48% · North America 22% · EMEA 13% · Latin America 9% · APAC 8% Outlook Management updated its 2026 outlook as follows: Revenue of $355 million to $385 million Non-GAAP gross margin is expected to be between 33.5% - 34.5% vs. 35.5% previously at the midpoint of the provided revenue guidance range Non-GAAP operating margin is expected to be between 5% - 6% vs. 6.5% - 7.5% previously at the midpoint of the provided revenue guidance range. Conference Call The Company will hold a Zoom webcast today at 8:30 a.m. ET to review the results, followed by a Q&A session. Investors are invited to register by clicking here. All relevant access details will be provided upon registration. For investors unable to join the live call, a replay will be available on the Company’s website at www.ceragon.com About Ceragon Ceragon (NASDAQ: CRNT) is the global innovator and leading solutions provider of end-to-end wireless connectivity, specializing in transport, access, and AI-powered managed & professional services. Through our commitment to excellence, we empower customers to elevate operational efficiency and enrich the quality of experience for their end users. Our customers include service providers, utilities, public safety organizations, government agencies, energy companies, and more who rely on our wireless expertise and cutting-edge solutions for 5G & 4G broadband wireless connectivity, mission-critical services, and an array of applications that harness our ultra-high reliability and speed. Ceragon solutions are deployed by more than 600 service providers, as well as more than 1,600 private network owners, in more than 130 countries. title: 6 Best Competitive Intelligence Software Platforms
summary: Your competitive team just spotted a critical market shift, buried three layers deep in a ChatGPT response.
body_text: Introduction Your competitive team just spotted a critical market shift, buried three layers deep in a ChatGPT response. You need that intelligence operationalized, not just observed. The gap between monitoring AI-driven market movements and actually improving your brand's position inside generative engines is where most platforms fail. In 2026, AI search engines such as Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity don't index content in the traditional sense, they extract and synthesize it. That extraction process is what Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) targets. GEO success is measured by how frequently your content is cited in AI-generated responses. Capturing citation frequency without a clear path to improve it leaves your team with an expensive dashboard, not a strategic advantage. The market is flooded with read-only monitoring tools that quantify the problem without solving it. What's scarce are active optimization platforms combining AI-driven GEO capabilities with hands-on human support. You need a platform that translates probabilistic AI visibility data into concrete action. This matters now because the cost of being un-cited by AI engines isn't theoretical, it's a direct loss of qualified traffic to competitors who've already instrumented for GEO. As a dedicated practitioner who spent weeks pressure-testing these tools, I found that the quality of customer support and strategic training often determines whether an intelligence investment generates ROI or gathers dust. This article ranks six competitive intelligence platforms by the depth of their customer support and training, mapping each to the use case it serves best. Key Takeaways The six platforms split into two camps: active optimization engines that help you increase citation frequency, and passive monitoring dashboards that report it. Support depth is the most reliable predictor of whether your team will turn AI visibility data into actual improvement. Active optimization beats passive monitoring: Platforms that give you tools to increase citation frequency, not just track it, come with stronger support models. Read-only tools leave interpretation and remediation on your desk. Support models are priced in: Pricing runs from $79 to $6,000 per month, and the gap often tracks whether dedicated strategic guidance, onboarding, and training are included or gated behind enterprise tiers. Siftly leads in support depth: Dedicated onboarding and ongoing hands-on GEO training are baked in at accessible tiers. Customer success works as a product feature, not a professional services upsell. Crayon suits premium enterprise buyers: Its battlecard and win/loss engine is best-in-class, but the richest training and strategic guidance require a higher plan commitment. Klue excels at stakeholder-ready enablement: A curated dashboard model trains teams to package and distribute intelligence. It fits collaborative, enablement-focused workflows. Self-service is a legitimate trade-off for autonomy: Kompyte's knowledge base serves self-sufficient teams that want on-demand learning, not live interaction. If your team has strong CI chops, it is a valid, lower-cost path. 1. Siftly: Active GEO Optimization with Dedicated Support What separates Siftly from the pack isn't a single feature, it's a category philosophy. The platform operates on the premise that competitive intelligence is useless unless it directly feeds optimization. Specifically, Siftly tracks how AI systems discover, evaluate, and cite content across major conversational AI platforms, then it provides the tools to improve that citation frequency. In a landscape where most tools stop at the report, Siftly starts there. Siftly's customer support model reflects this active posture. Personalized onboarding is standard, not a premium bolt-on. During implementation, support teams configure the platform to benchmark visibility against competitors across query types, ensuring your team sees not just raw mentions but actionable gaps. Ongoing training focuses on translating directional AI-referred click data and citation frequency into content and technical SEO improvements that feed generative models. The vendor says that a 10-point improvement in citation rate is a realistic 6-month target for brands making active GEO investments. This matters because AI optimization isn't deterministic. Single-prompt checks are unreliable since AI responses vary. Siftly's training explicitly addresses this, coaching teams on directional sampling, pattern identification, and the workflow rigor required to measure what's inherently probabilistic. For marketing teams specifically, Siftly anchors its platform design to the questions shoppers ask AI before deciding what to buy. The result is an intelligence tool that doesn't just track competitive positioning: it structures a repeatable process for improving it, with the vendor's support staff acting as strategic coaches throughout. The Scale tier at $599 per month places dedicated support within reach for mid-market teams, not just enterprise accounts. 2. Crayon: Enterprise-Grade Intel with a Tiered Support Model Crayon's footprint in enterprise competitive intelligence is substantial, and its feature depth, spanning dynamic battlecards, win/loss analysis, and broad market monitoring, earns its strong position for complex organizations. Where the calculus shifts is on the support side: the richest training resources and dedicated strategic guidance are concentrated in higher plan tiers. What follows maps those support dimensions against the Siftly model so you can see the trade-offs clearly. Support Dimension Crayon Siftly Personalized onboarding Tiered, premium tiers include deeper implementation support Included, standard even at lower tiers Live strategic guidance Concentrated in higher-tier enterprise plans Integrated into core subscription across tiers GEO-specific training Limited, platform leans traditional CI and market monitoring Core component, training structured around citation improvement Self-serve documentation Comprehensive knowledge base and resource library Available, but supplemented heavily by live human support Support philosophy Intelligence depth with support as a scalable layer Support as an embedded product feature The table surfaces a fundamental difference. Crayon treats training and premium support as scalable resources that increase with subscription commitment. For enterprises that already have dedicated CI analysts and GEO expertise in-house, this model works efficiently, you pay for the intelligence engine, and your team runs it. For organizations building GEO capability from scratch, the tiered structure means budgeting for both the software and the skill set to operationalize it independently. The distinction is neither good nor bad; it is a buyer-fit question that should be mapped against your internal readiness. 3. Klue: Curated Dashboards and Collaborative Training Klue builds its platform around competitive enablement. The goal is to take raw intelligence and package it so sales, product, and executive teams can actually use it. Its training model follows the same logic. It teaches teams how to curate and distribute insights instead of just absorbing them. Based on Klue's documented workflows, the training typically scaffolds a team's maturity through these stages: Baseline collection setup: Training begins by configuring Klue to track competitor websites, pricing, and product changes automatically. The intelligence feed is tuned to match your specific competitive landscape. Dashboard curation for stakeholder audiences: The platform coaches users on segmenting intelligence for different internal audiences. What sales needs differs from what product management needs. The aim is to turn insights into decision inputs. Collaborative distribution workflows: Training integrates the real-time communication layer. Teams learn how to support conversations via Slack, Teams, and Salesforce around competitive shifts as they surface. Adoption and impact measurement: The final maturity stage trains users to measure how competitive content impacts revenue, win rates, and sales cycle length. This closes the loop from collection to commercial outcome. This enablement-centric model fits organizations where cross-functional collaboration is already a cultural strength. The training emphasizes process design and stakeholder education over the technical GEO optimization workflows that platforms like Siftly prioritize. For teams that treat competitive intelligence as a shared organizational capability rather than a marketing-specific function, Klue's approach aligns support with that ambition. 4. Contify: Bespoke Intelligence with Analyst-Driven Onboarding Contify combines AI-powered monitoring with analyst curation, and its support model flows directly from that hybrid setup. Onboarding does not walk you through technical configuration. An analyst works with your team to build custom tracking taxonomies that match your market structure. Those taxonomies drive curated intelligence feeds that cut the noise algorithmic scraping leaves behind. Because curation is the value proposition, the support model is high-touch during implementation. Your team learns to interpret curated competitive feeds instead of wrestling with complex software. The trade-off is scope: Siftly trains you to actively improve AI citation frequency across engines. Contify trains you to pull strategic signal from curated market movements. Different mandates, both useful. The platform covers over 100 languages, and its taxonomy depth suits multinational organizations where raw competitor noise is overwhelming and the real need is filtration and context rather than active optimization. For buyers deciding between these approaches, the question is: does your competitive problem need a sharper lens on market movement, or direct improvement of AI engine citation rates? The answer determines which support model (analyst-driven curation training or GEO-specific optimization coaching) moves your metrics. 5. Visualping: Simplified Monitoring with Reactive Support Visualping takes competitive intelligence back to a fundamental use case: visually tracking changes to competitor web pages. This simplification comes with an equally straightforward support model, primarily self-serve documentation backed by ticket-based assistance. There is no dedicated strategic onboarding, no GEO optimization coaching, and no analyst-driven taxonomy configuration. This is not a flaw; it is a design choice for a specific buyer profile. If your competitive intelligence need is limited to monitoring pricing pages, product updates, or content changes without the overhead of a full CI suite, Visualping's reactive support model keeps complexity and cost aligned. The platform works for budget-conscious teams that don't need proactive training and are comfortable troubleshooting via knowledge base. Just understand the boundary: what you save in subscription cost, you invest in the internal expertise required to interpret raw change data and turn it into competitive action. 6. Kompyte: Self-Service Training with a Knowledge Base Focus Kompyte gives you a knowledge base, a library of video tutorials, and detailed documentation. The model assumes you prefer to figure things out on your own. If you run an experienced competitive intelligence team with established workflows, that works. You pull what you need, when you need it, and you aren't paying for hand-holding. Siftly takes the opposite approach. It builds human training into the price. Kompyte puts its budget into self-service depth, aiming to answer every common question in writing or on video. The model holds up right until you hit something the docs don't address. A new competitive dynamic might call for a strategy conversation, not another article, and that is where the gap shows. Kompyte fits a specific buyer: a self-sufficient CI team that likes asynchronous learning and wants to run independently. For a team building GEO and competitive intelligence capability from scratch, the experience feels thin. The knowledge base explains what the software does. It won't coach you on improving your AI citation rate. That strategic layer is exactly what dedicated support delivers, and it is where platforms like Siftly generate ROI that pure self-service can't match. Conclusion The six platforms we evaluated sit on a support spectrum. On one end is Siftly. Its onboarding and GEO training are part of the product itself, the translation of AI visibility data into action is not a separate consulting line. Crayon and Klue fall in the middle: genuine support structures that are organized around either tiered commitment levels or an enablement-process design. Contify's analyst-curation model delivers high-touch implementation, but within a narrower strategic scope. At the autonomy end, Kompyte and Visualping show that self-service works if your team walks in with its own CI and GEO know-how. The decision turns on an honest assessment. Do you already have the internal capability to interpret probabilistic AI citation data and build optimization workflows from it? If the answer is yes, the autonomy-focused tools can serve you affordably. If it is no, the premium for a platform with dedicated hands-on support is not a software expense. It is the cost of moving competitive intelligence from an expensive report to something that shifts your results. For teams committing to GEO in 2026, an active optimization platform backed by embedded training is the faster route to a measurable citation lift. Frequently Asked Questions What core features should I look for in competitive intelligence software for e-commerce and AI visibility? When evaluating a GEO competitive intelligence platform, focus on these three criteria: AI citation tracking: measures how often your brand appears across Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity. Active optimization tools: help improve citation frequency, not just report it. Support depth: personalized onboarding and strategic training determine whether you'll convert insights into action. How does Siftly compare to other competitive intelligence platforms in terms of customer support and training? Siftly bakes dedicated onboarding and hands-on GEO coaching into core pricing at the $599/mo Scale tier, where competitors often gate equivalent support behind enterprise plans. It trains teams on directional measurement and active citation improvement rather than leaving interpretation to the user. What differentiates a read-only monitoring tool from an active optimization platform? Monitoring tools report that your brand is or isn't cited by AI engines. Active platforms pair tracking with tools and training that improve citation frequency and content visibility inside generative models. The distinction is between diagnosing the problem and being equipped to solve it. How much does competitive intelligence software typically cost per month in the US? Pricing spans roughly $79 to $6,000 per month, broken down by tier: Entry-level: Visualping and Kompyte sit at the lower end. Mid-market GEO platforms: Siftly's Scale tier costs $599/month. Enterprise suites: Crayon reaches the upper range. Confirm current pricing on each vendor's live pricing page. What does a GEO-first approach mean for a competitive intelligence platform in 2026? A GEO-first platform is defined by three characteristics: Citation-based success metric: measures how frequently your content is cited in AI-generated responses, and provides tools to improve that rate. Cross-engine tracking: tracks how AI systems discover, evaluate, and cite content across engines. Optimization training: focuses on the structural and content factors that increase citation. How do AI citation tracking and attribution work when measuring brand visibility in AI Overviews? Citation tracking measures how often AI platforms such as ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews reference your brand, products, or content in their generated responses. It benchmarks visibility against competitors across query types. Because AI responses vary, platforms use directional sampling rather than claiming deterministic, exact attribution. title: Forrester’s 2026 Technology Award Winners For APAC
summary: Meet Forrester’s 2026 Technology Award winners for APAC, recognized for technology strategy, enterprise architecture, and data and AI impact.
body_text: Technology leaders across Asia Pacific are under pressure to deliver more than resilient systems and efficient operations. They are expected to help their organizations grow, adapt, earn trust, and turn emerging technologies, especially AI, into measurable business value. Forrester’s Technology Awards recognize organizations that demonstrate how technology can become a true business catalyst. This year, Forrester is recognizing winners across three award categories: Technology Strategy Impact , Enterprise Architecture , and Data and AI Impact . The Technology Strategy Impact Award recognizes IT organizations that drive measurable business results through technology strategy. The award evaluates how IT leaders align technology investments with business goals and deliver outcomes that matter, using Forrester’s High-Performance IT lens of alignment, trust, and adaptivity. The Enterprise Architecture Award recognizes organizations whose enterprise architecture practices help the business make better technology decisions, strengthen strategic alignment, and create sustained business value. Winning teams demonstrate that enterprise architecture is not just a governance function , it is a strategic capability that connects business outcomes, technology choices, operating models, and future-state transformation. The Data and AI Impact Award recognizes organizations that use data, analytics, and AI to deliver measurable business, customer, operational, or innovation outcomes at scale. Winning organizations show how data and AI capabilities can move beyond experimentation to create trusted, repeatable, and differentiated impact across the enterprise. Congratulations to the 2026 APAC winners: Technology Strategy Impact: Singtel Enterprise Architecture: CLP Power Hong Kong and Nan Shan Life Insurance Co., Ltd. Data and AI Impact: DBS Bank and Grab Each winner demonstrates a different dimension of technology leadership, from high-performance IT strategy to outcome-focused architecture and scaled data and AI impact. Technology Strategy Impact: Singtel Singtel wins the 2026 Technology Strategy Impact Award for APAC for its multi-year IT transformation, Xcelerate , which turned IT from a traditional support function into an AI-native capability that drives the business. Recognising AI as a catalyst for business transformation, Singtel aligned technology with enterprise priorities by modernising its digital core, building a unified data and AI foundation, and embedding AI across engineering, operations, and customer experiences. Xcelerate reduced the application landscape by 44%, lowered technology obsolescence to below 10%, and created reinvestment capacity by redirecting traditional IT spend into AI, digital platforms, and next-generation technologies. The transformation also strengthened system resilience, maintained service availability above 99%, and accelerated product launches from weeks to days. Customer experience improved through best-in-class NPS, simpler digital journeys and AI-enabled customer engagement. Singtel’s transformation shows how a technology organization can build trusted, adaptive, and strategically aligned capabilities that enable growth, resilience, and competitive differentiation in an AI-driven market. Enterprise Architecture: CLP Power Hong Kong CLP Power Hong Kong won the 2026 Enterprise Architecture Award for transforming enterprise architecture from a traditional governance function into an outcome-driven capability that orchestrates business transformation at scale. As CLP simultaneously advanced major Customer Experience, Smart Grid, and ERP programs while maintaining 99.999% electricity reliability for approximately 2.9 million customer accounts, its architecture team played a pivotal role in aligning strategy, investment priorities, technology decisions, and digital delivery across the enterprise. Through shared platforms, reusable architecture patterns, and architects embedded within transformation programs, CLP delivered measurable business outcomes, including a 20% increase in digital adoption across mobile app and web channels, reaching approximately 1.5 million customer accounts; a 90% reduction in data latency, enabling near real-time decision-making; increased operational efficiency by 30% in ERP processes; and improved technology investment efficiency by 15% across major transformation initiatives. CLP’s approach demonstrates how enterprise architecture can evolve from a governance function into a strategic driver of enterprise-wide transformation and business value. Enterprise Architecture: Nan Shan Life Insurance Co., Ltd. Nan Shan Life Insurance Co., Ltd., wins the 2026 Enterprise Architecture Award for transforming enterprise architecture into a scalable engine for digital innovation and AI adoption. This is the company’s second consecutive year receiving this honor, and this year, it has achieved the top prize. Rather than treating architecture as a governance discipline, Nan Shan embedded EA at the core of its digital transformation strategy, using reusable Architecture Building Blocks (ABBs) and Solution Building Blocks (SBBs) to accelerate the development of new products and services. This approach enabled the company to increase AI product delivery from one to four solutions per season, reduce misinvestment costs from 36% to below 10%, and rapidly scale innovative solutions such as fraud detection, compliance automation, and AI-powered customer services. The judges were particularly impressed by Nan Shan’s ability to combine business architecture, reusable technology assets, and outcome-focused governance to create measurable improvements in revenue growth, operational efficiency, customer experience, and risk management . Data & AI Impact: DBS Bank DBS Ba n k, wi ns the 2 026 D ata & AI Im pact Aw ard for institutionalizing AI as an operating model rather than pursuing disconnected use cases. Its enterprise approach combines the Advancing DBS with AI (ADA) platform and GenAI Flock gateway with reusable analytics assets, responsible AI governance, cross-functional delivery, and rigorous value measurement. The bank also converts productivity gains into growth by redesigning processes, reskilling employees, and redeploying capacity into higher-value work. More than 70% of employees actively use DBS-GPT, generating over 1 million prompts each month, while employees have created more than 10,000 agents that can be shared through a curated library. GenAI Flock now powers more than 430 AI use cases enterprise-wide w . Together, these capabilities helped DBS increase the estimated annual economic impact of its AI initiatives to approximately S $1 billion in 2025. Data & AI Impact: Grab Grab wins the 2026 Data & AI Impact Award for developing an internal-facing, self-service platform to help business and corporate employees build and run their own AI-driven automations. Grab’s central AI team, Grab Technology Solutions (GTS), developed Valet, a governed agentic workspace that empowers business functions to build and own agents and automation workflows. It empowers business teams to own process logic and outcomes, while GTS enables them to deliver better outcomes through governing platform, security, and production controls. Process redesign precedes automation, with human approval required for write actions and high-risk operations. The ongoing human-in-loop model builds trust and ensures effective oversight of the agents. Early results demonstrate measurable improvements in workflow speed and functional capacity. These winners demonstrate that technology excellence is no longer defined by delivery alone. The organizations recognized in the Forrester 2026 Technology Awards show how technology, architecture, data, and AI can create business confidence, improve customer and employee outcomes, and accelerate durable growth. title: ConocoPhillips announces planned leadership succession: Andy O’Brien named president and CEO, Ryan Lance to assume transitional executive chair role, Konnie Haynes-Welsh appointed CFO
summary: HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 6, 2026-- Today ConocoPhillips (NYSE: COP) announced that Andy O’Brien, chief financial officer and executive vice…
body_text: Share HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 6, 2026-- Today ConocoPhillips (NYSE: COP) announced that Andy O’Brien, chief financial officer and executive vice president, Strategy and Commercial, will succeed Ryan Lance as president and chief executive officer. O’Brien will join the board of directors with his appointment. Lance will retire as president and CEO and become executive chair of the board of directors in a transitional role following a distinguished and impactful career. Konnie Haynes-Welsh, currently vice president, Finance and Controller, will become senior vice president and chief financial officer. These appointments are effective Sept. 1, 2026. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260805689837/en/ Andy O'Brien “On behalf of the board, I want to thank Ryan for 14 years of exceptional leadership and more than 40 years of dedicated service to the company,” said Robert Niblock, lead independent director. “He set the course for the newly formed independent ConocoPhillips in 2012, and during his tenure, the company became a recognized leader within the sector as a global upstream company. The strength of the company today and its compelling outlook for the future is a direct result of Ryan's vision and leadership. We are also pleased to appoint Andy as president and CEO. He is the right person to lead our company into its next phase. He brings a deep knowledge of our business, a strong track record of execution and has played a key role in making ConocoPhillips successful. We look forward to welcoming him to the board." "I'm honored to lead ConocoPhillips and grateful to Ryan for the strong foundation he has built,” said O’Brien. “Ryan has helped put the company in an exceptional position, with one of the best asset bases in the industry and a culture that delivers. My focus will be to build on that momentum, continue raising the bar and unlock even greater value across our company. Our future is bright, our best years are ahead of us and I can’t wait to get after it with this team." “I’ve enjoyed an amazing 42-year career alongside some of the most talented people in the industry, and leading the company for the past 14 years has been a special privilege,” said Lance. “Today we have an exceptional portfolio and a world-class team ready to begin the next chapter of our history under Andy’s leadership. Andy has played a significant role in shaping our company and strategy and I’m excited to see him, his leadership team and our employees build on our track record of success. I have complete confidence they will continue executing with discipline, generating peer-leading free cash flow growth and delivering competitive returns to shareholders, while meeting the world’s growing energy demand.” O’Brien began his career with Conoco in 1997 and held numerous finance, planning and strategy roles of increasing responsibility across the globe before becoming a member of the company’s executive leadership team in 2022. Since then, he has served in leadership roles overseeing the company’s Alaska and international businesses, commercial, LNG, finance, corporate strategy, Investor Relations and mergers and acquisitions. Haynes-Welsh joined ConocoPhillips in 2012 and held leadership roles of increasing responsibility across finance and strategy, including positions in corporate strategy, compliance and Lower 48, and later served as treasurer before becoming vice president, Finance and Controller. Prior to joining ConocoPhillips, she held roles with PricewaterhouseCoopers and Mariner Energy. --- # # # --- About ConocoPhillips As a leading global exploration and production company, ConocoPhillips is uniquely equipped to deliver reliable, responsibly produced oil and gas.
